items.title: Living Through the Heat: Lifestyle changes you must make
items.description: By Josephine Agbonkhese STEPPING outside lately can sometimes feel like walking into an oven. Before long, you’re burning up, sweating, feeling thirsty and wishing you could return to the comfort of your home. While this may be a familiar experience for many Nigerians, rising global temperatures are making the heat a more serious health concern. A recent Climate Impact Lab report projected that Nigeria could record 31,400 additional heat-related deaths between September 2026 and February 2027 as the El Niño weather pattern intensifies. Beyond fatalities, extreme heat can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion, heatstroke, headaches, dizziness, fainting, skin rashes, sunburn, poor sleep and difficulty concentrating. Although this is only a projection, the warning underscores the need to take extreme heat seriously by adjusting our everyday habits. Know When Heat Is Becoming Dangerous Severe weakness, dizziness, headaches, nausea or heavy sweating may indicate heat exhaustion and should not be ignored. Move the affected person to a cooler place, loosen any unnecessary clothing and help them cool down. If they are fully alert and can swallow safely, offer them water. Heatstroke is a medical emergency. Call emergency medical services immediately and begin cooling the person while waiting for help. Do not give fluids to someone who is confused or unconscious. Pay particular attention to older adults, young children and people with health conditions such as diabetes. Drink Water Before You Feel Thirsty Keep safe drinking water within reach, whether you’re at your desk, in transit or at the market. Drink regularly rather than waiting until you feel thirsty. Water-rich foods such as watermelon, oranges and cucumber can also contribute to hydration, but they should not replace drinking water. People on medically prescribed fluid restrictions should follow their healthcare professional’s advice. Dress for the Weather Loose-fitting clothing made from lightweight, breathable fabrics such as cotton and linen can help you stay cooler. Choose lighter colours and comfortable footwear where possible. A wide-brimmed hat, sunglasses and an umbrella can provide additional protection outdoors. If your work requires formal attire, opt for breathable fabrics and lighter layers. Rethink Your Daily Schedule Must that errand happen at noon? Could your walk, outdoor exercise or market visit be scheduled for earlier in the morning or later in the evening? Where possible, plan strenuous activities for cooler parts of the day and reduce exposure to direct sunlight during the hottest hours. If you work outdoors, take regular breaks in shaded or cool areas. Parents should also pay attention to children’s outdoor play, sports and school activities. Never leave a child alone in a parked vehicle, even for a few minutes. Make Your Home More Comfortable Not everyone can afford air conditioning, particularly given the cost of electricity. However, keeping curtains or blinds closed to block direct sunlight during the hottest hours can help. Where safe and practical, open windows when the outdoor air is cooler to improve ventilation, and use fans to circulate air. Also, avoid activities that generate unnecessary indoor heat during the hottest hours. Wear Sunscreen Protecting your skin is another important part of managing hot weather. Apply a broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen with an SPF of 30 or higher to exposed skin before going outdoors. Reapply it at least every two hours and after swimming or heavy sweating, following the product instructions. Sunscreen does not replace shade, protective clothing or measures to limit prolonged exposure to intense sunlight. Combine these precautions to reduce the risk of sunburn and harmful ultraviolet radiation exposure. WHAT SCHOOLS, WORKPLACES AND GOVERNMENT MUST DO SCHOOLS must reconsider strenuous outdoor activities, sports and assemblies during the hottest periods of the day while ensuring that pupils have access to drinking water and cool spaces. EMPLOYERS , particularly those whose workers spend long hours outdoors, should adjust work schedules where possible, provide adequate breaks and take heat warnings seriously. GOVERNMENT must also make public spaces safer for people who are exposed to the sun daily. This includes providing adequate shade at bus stops and motor parks, where commuters and transport workers often spend considerable time waiting in the heat. items.title: Mahama says social media criticism helps him become a better leader
items.description: President John Mahama has disclosed that social media platforms, including TikTok, help him pick up public complaints and feedback on government performance, which he forwards to ministers for attention. He says criticism from citizens, regardless of their political affiliations, is an important tool for improving governance and helping him become a better leader. Speaking during an engagement with the Ghanaian Community in Moscow, President Mahama said he does not take offence when citizens accuse his administration of heading in the wrong direction, insisting that constructive criticism helps him identify problems and demand answers from his ministers. “I don’t mind if people tell me that I’m leading the country in the wrong direction. I’m trying to do my best. Criticism helps me to do better,” he said. The President disclosed that he sometimes comes across complaints social media and contacts ministers directly to seek explanations about developments in their respective sectors. “Sometimes I go on the media and I see something, and I call the minister and I say, ‘Hey, my friend, what is happening in your sector?'” he recounted. He assured citizens that their videos and complaints do not go unnoticed. “So all your TikToks and things, don’t think I don’t see them. I see them,” President Mahama said. To illustrate how social media feedback informs government action, he cited a complaint about a bridge in the Ashanti Region which had reportedly been affected by illegal mining activities and washed away. The President said he saw the information on social media and immediately forwarded it to the minister responsible, requesting that the situation be died According to him, the minister subsequently visited the location and reported that a blocked channel was contributing to the problem, with an excavator being deployed to clear it and allow water to flow. “That is how you solve some of these things,” he said. President Mahama believes the growing influence of new media presents an opportunity for government to receive information directly from citizens and respond to challenges as they emerge. “The new media is an advantage because it gives us information in real time,” he added. He urged citizens to speak up whenever they identify warning signs in the country’s governance, stressing that holding leaders accountable should transcend partisan political considerations. “The more we see the danger signs that somebody is leading us the wrong way, we must, all of us, not based on partisan leanings, all of us must say no, we’re not going in the right direction,” he said.

items.title: From ‘Miracle Girl’ to Purpose: How Esther Longe turned survival into life of impact
items.description: *SHE survived the 2006 crash that claimed 96 lives, battled survivor’s guilt, and spent a decade building a career in marketing before embracing a divine call to ministry. Today, she is redefining leadership through faith, strategy and legacy. By Nkiruka Nnorom The first thing that hits you about Dr Esther Longe is how ordinary she looks. No burn scars. No limp. No visible reminder of a tragedy that wiped out 96 lives in minutes. Only a small scratch. A literal scratch, she calls it. On October 29, 2006, 21-year-old Esther was aboard ADC Airlines Flight 053 from Abuja to Sokoto. The Boeing 737-2B7 crashed shortly after take-off after encountering wind shear, broke up, and burst into flames in a cornfield near Tungar Madaki village, Abuja. 20 YEARS AFTER THE ADC AIR CRASH There were 105 souls on board — 100 passengers and five crew members. Ninety-six died, including the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Maccido; his son, Senator Badamasi Maccido; and Deputy Governor Alhaji Garba Muhammed. Nine survived. Of all the survivors, Esther Kemmer Amoda, now Longe, was the only one without physical injuries. The burden of a miracle Newspapers the next morning called her the Miracle Girl. Television vans camped outside her home. Everybody said the same thing: “God has saved your life for a reason.” At 21, she did not want a reason. She wanted to disappear. “From the onset, I understood that my survival came with a responsibility. But it came with panic attacks and survivor’s guilt,” she tells Weekender. “As a 21-year-old, that was daunting. I did not know what that purpose was. I did not think I had done anything to deserve being saved or singled out.” The years she ran For the next ten years, she ran. She ran into lecture halls and boardrooms. She bagged a BSc in Mass Communication from the University of Lagos, a master’s in Marketing from the University of South Wales, UK, a master’s in Research, and a PhD in Marketing, both from the University of Bath, UK. She became a trained marketing strategist, working with some of the biggest global brands — PwC, GTBank, Pizza Express, and Wrigley’s. She served as a Super Mentor for FCMB SheVentures and a facilitator for the Africa Green Grant Award. She was on track to become a Chief Marketing Officer at a Fortune 500 company. She wanted to be known for what she built, not what she survived. “If I am being honest, I ran and hid,” she confesses. “If you look at me, you would not know I had been through such an experience. It was easy to hide. I did not want to be known for something I had nothing to do with. I wanted to be known for what I had accomplished.” But purpose does not need permission. People who lost loved ones on that flight began to find her. Not to blame her, but to connect. In their eyes, she saw a question she could not run from: If you were saved, what are you doing with the life taken from us? “I have had the opportunity to interact with people who lost loved ones on that flight. Those encounters reinforced my desire to live intentionally. I cannot bring their loved ones back, but I hope when they see how I am living, they will believe some good can come out of such a horrible experience.” The disruption In December 2016, exactly ten years after she began building a new identity, came the disruption she never planned. God told her to leave marketing and minister full-time. “I was very upset because that was not the life I had planned for myself,” she says. “I had written my first life plan at 19. I am Type A. I prided myself on control. Here was God asking me to walk on water with no blueprint.” She surrendered, albeit reluctantly at first. Then, wholly. What followed is a portfolio she never imagined. Today, she describes herself as a transformative leader whose mission is to reconnect people to an intimate relationship with God and free individuals, families, and nations from the strongholds of their past. She is a speaker, author, teacher, marketplace pastor, trainer, and coach. She is the lead coach for the Unicorn Programme, her flagship coaching programme, through which she helps people embrace their God-given uniqueness, break limiting beliefs, heal trauma, and align with God’s will to shine in every area of life. From strategy to sanctuary She channels that assignment through five ministry expressions. God in Real Life Outreach helps people experience intimacy with God in everyday life. Broken serves the broken-hearted who seek to reconnect with God after life’s challenges. The Alternative Business School (TABS) is a life business school for believers in Christ, teaching them how to do business, govern, and minister with integrity. The 7000 Movement celebrates individuals who lead, govern, and minister with integrity, righteousness, and justice. Adullam Fellowship is a monthly virtual gathering for kings and priests in the marketplace — a place for God’s army to be refreshed. Her edge is her unique ability to simplify complex issues. Faith meets strategy. Marketing precision meets ministry passion. Whole Leadership: Her survival code She calls her model Whole Leadership. It rests on three pillars: identity, radical candour, and authentic leadership. For her, it is not theory. It is a survival strategy. “I cannot separate my faith from who I am. I lead from values. I don’t just make business decisions; I make value-based business decisions. I don’t see people who work with me as employees. I see them as individuals entrusted to my care.” Vanguard News The post From ‘Miracle Girl’ to Purpose: How Esther Longe turned survival into life of impact appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Au Texas, Elon Musk a déversé presque autant d’argent dans la campagne sénatoriale que tout le camp démocrate
items.description: L’élection sénatoriale au Texas est devenue au cours de ce cycle électoral la campagne la plus chère de l’histoire des États-Unis. Selon nos calculs à partir des données disponibles au 27 octobre, 559 millions de dollars (362 millions côté républicain et 197 millions côté démocrate) ont été dépensés par les candidats et les groupes qui les soutiennent, primaires comprises. À lui seul, Elon Musk a financé environ 190 millions de dollars de dépenses, soit presque autant que l’ensemble des dépenses du camp démocrate. Le Parti républicain n’a pas perdu une élection sénatoriale au Texas depuis 1988, lorsque l’élu démocrate sortant, Lloyd Bentsen, avait remporté l’élection avec 59 % des voix. Le siège pour lequel Talarico fait actuellement campagne n’a quant à lui plus été occupé par un démocrate depuis 65 ans. Toutefois, les sondages agrégés par Nate Silver indiquent que Talarico disposerait d’une courte avance de 3 points sur Paxton au 29 octobre, ce qui suscite des inquiétudes parmi les principaux donateurs républicains et la direction du Parti. Trump lui-même s’est rendu au Texas mardi 27, à Lubbock puis à Waco, pour la troisième fois en un mois afin d’afficher son soutien à Ken Paxton. L’implication inédite de Musk dans la campagne sénatoriale au Texas s’explique notamment par les intérêts économiques qu’il a développés dans l’État : ses deux principales entreprises, Tesla et SpaceX, sont toutes deux basées au Texas, de même que sa fondation privée, la Musk Foundation, et plus de 90 sociétés et autres entités qui lui sont liées Elon Musk’s Secret Web of Companies in Texas », The New York Times , 27 février 2026.'> 4 . La majeure partie des dépenses financées par Musk et d’autres groupes de soutien à Paxton sont dédiées à la diffusion de publicités. Selon une étude publiée en 2021, un avantage de 2 millions de dollars de dépenses publicitaires télévisées sur son adversaire lors d’une campagne sénatoriale peut conduire à 10 000 votes supplémentaires – de quoi faire basculer plusieurs courses serrées The effect of television advertising in United States elections », American Political Science Review , 2022, vol. 116, n°2, p. 702-718.'> 5 . Les auteurs de l’étude estiment que lors de la présidentielle de 2016, un avantage de 10 millions de dollars dans un État aurait pu rapporter environ 27 000 voix, une marge qui aurait suffi à inverser le résultat dans cinq États (Nevada, Maine, Michigan, Wisconsin et New Hampshire). Au Texas, l’avantage publicitaire en faveur du candidat républicain au Sénat est de 138,6 millions de dollars pour l’élection générale, selon une analyse du New York Times à partir des données d’AdImpact : le camp républicain y dépense deux fois plus que le camp démocrate (268 millions contre 130 millions) Where the Parties Are Outspending Each Other in the Midterm Ad War », The New York Times , 28 octobre 2026.'> 6 . L’explosion des dépenses électorales par des individus s’explique par deux facteurs. Depuis la décision Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission rendue par la Cour suprême en 2010, les entreprises peuvent, en vertu du premier amendement, financer sans limite des dépenses électorales indépendantes des candidats. Dans la foulée, la justice fédérale a autorisé les individus à verser des sommes illimitées aux super PAC. Le développement de l’intelligence artificielle a fait exploser les fortunes des dirigeants d’entreprises technologiques : la fortune d’Elon Musk est estimée à plus de 920 milliards de dollars selon Bloomberg , soit trois fois plus qu’il y a cinq ans. L’article Au Texas, Elon Musk a déversé presque autant d’argent dans la campagne sénatoriale que tout le camp démocrate est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: CAA, NFA, Copyright Ghana to lead dialogue on creatives’ pension scheme
items.description: The Creative Arts Agency (CAA), National Film Authority (NFA) and Copyright Ghana will lead stakeholder discussions on a sustainable pension and social security programme for Ghanaian creative professionals. The dialogue, dubbed “My Art, My Ark! Dialogue”, is scheduled for Monday, 2 November 2026, at the British Council in Accra, beginning at 12:30 p.m. The initiative is being organised by the CAA and NFA in partnership with Copyright Ghana and its Collective Management Organisations (CMOs): CopyGhana, ARSOG and GHAMRO, with support from the British Council, Accra. The engagement seeks to develop a roadmap towards establishing a social security programme that responds to the financial security and long-term welfare needs of Ghanaian creative professionals. Pension schemes provide a mechanism for individuals to build financial security for retirement through contributions accumulated during their working lives. However, creative professionals often face distinctive employment and income challenges, including freelance engagements, irregular earnings and limited access to conventional employment benefits. These realities raise an important question: How can Ghana develop a sustainable pension arrangement that accommodates the diverse working conditions and income patterns of its creative workforce? Beyond individual contributions, the proposed initiative brings into focus the role of government, relevant public institutions, industry organisations and other stakeholders in creating the policy, regulatory and administrative conditions necessary to make such a programme possible. The dialogue is expected to provide a platform for brainstorming practical, inclusive and sustainable approaches to extending social security opportunities to creatives across Ghana’s diverse creative arts and cultural industries. The initiative is linked to a manifesto commitment under the Black Star Experience to establish and promote “career security through legal and financial protection and mass pension schemes”. Translating this commitment into a workable programme will require coordination among relevant government agencies, collective management organisations, creative industry associations and the professionals who stand to benefit from the proposed arrangement. Key considerations include how creatives with irregular incomes can participate, the potential contribution structure, the institutional framework for implementation and the measures required to ensure the programme’s long-term sustainability. The stakeholder dialogue is intended to contribute to a roadmap for addressing these issues and advancing discussions towards a social security framework tailored to the realities of Ghana’s creative economy. As Ghana continues to explore ways of strengthening its creative economy, the proposed dialogue places an important issue on the industry agenda: ensuring that the people whose talents, ideas and intellectual contributions generate cultural and economic value can also work towards a more financially secure future.

items.title: Namibia President urges Africa to harness natural resources, youth for global influence
items.description: Namibian President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah says Africa must harness its vast natural resources and youthful population to strengthen its economic power and influence global decisions, rather than allow others to determine the continent’s future. She argues that Africa’s population of more than a billion people and its rich natural resources give the continent considerable economic leverage, which could be better utilised through stronger regional cooperation and increased trade among African countries. In an interview on Diplomatic Affairs with Harriet Nartey on Joy Prime, President Nandi-Ndaitwah said Africa must recognise its strengths and take greater responsibility for shaping the rules governing its participation in the global economy. “I believe that Africa needs to recognise their strength. First and foremost, we are a useful continent as we are now, and that is our biggest resource. That is complemented by our natural resources,” she said. The Namibian leader believes the continent must move beyond dependence on decisions made by external powers and build the confidence to set its own economic priorities. “Africa can take its own decisions and defend their decisions. And let others come in, if they want to come in,” she stated. President Nandi-Ndaitwah said Africa’s large population represents a significant market that could promote trade, strengthen local industries, and attract partners seeking to participate in the continent’s economic growth. She called for a stronger African Continental Free Trade Area, arguing that deeper economic integration would encourage countries to trade more among themselves and strengthen their collective position in the global marketplace. “If you really will see that we have been squeezed in this global village, and we strengthened our continental free trade area, and really decide to trade among ourselves, the others who come and join us,” she said. The President also questioned the tendency of African countries to approach international trade negotiations using rules and frameworks developed elsewhere, rather than defining arrangements that reflect the continent’s priorities. She cited rules of origin as an example, suggesting African countries should consider how to shape such rules to serve their interests. Diplomatic Affairs with Harriet Nartey is aired every Sunday at 7:30 pm on Joy Prime

items.title: N70,000 relief: Ajaero blasts TUC over rejection, as OPS sets condition for minimum wage
items.description: By Victor AhiumaYoung & Juliet Umeh The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has blasted its sister central Labour organisation, the Trade Union Congress, TUC, of Nigeria, for rejecting the negotiated N70,000 transport allowance for workers, describing the relief as a significant intervention to cushion the effects of rising petrol prices and the escalating cost of living. NLC President, Mr. Joe Ajaero, also challenged the TUC to negotiate better benefits for its members rather than criticise an agreement it did not participate in negotiating This comes as Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association, NECA, warned that organised private-sector employers cannot be bound by minimum wage agreements reached between the Federal Government and organised labour without their participation and concurrence, insisting that employers must have an equal voice in the negotiation process. Speaking on Channels Television, yesterday, Ajaero said: “Nigerian workers were suffering; no intervention, nothing, and we have pushed with the threat of strike. We almost went on strike to get something, and then we got this.” Describing the agreement as a landmark achievement, Ajaero said: “Between now and the next six months, this is a landmark achievement,” insisting that workers must not be left worse off when the allowance expires. On the disagreement with the TUC, Ajaero expressed surprise at its criticism, saying “The agreement was not signed by TUC, and you don’t kick against something that you didn’t negotiate. “My appeal is that they (TUC) should go and ask for something higher. Let them ask for one million naira if they want. “Is it better that they don’t get anything?” Ajaero maintained that the intervention could serve as a benchmark for further negotiations involving workers across different employment categories. Ajaero warned that the six-month allowance must not expire without a new minimum wage arrangement that reflects prevailing economic realities. He argued that future wage negotiations must consider rising transportation costs, food prices, housing and other necessities. “We have to find a way out of it. It is not in favour of government to now stop paying and then there is no new minimum wage and there is nothing new,” he said. Efforts to get the TUC to respond to Ajaero’s latest position were unsuccessful. The TUC Secretary-General, Nuhu Toro, answered his call but said he was driving and promised to call back as soon as he arrived at his destination. However, he had yet to do so as of the time of filing this report. Subsequent calls to his phone went unanswered. OPS fires warning Meanwhile, the Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association, NECA, has warned that organised private-sector employers cannot be bound by minimum wage agreements reached between the Federal Government and organised labour without their participation and concurrence, insisting that employers must have an equal voice in the negotiation process. NECA in its statement said: “We, the Voice of Organised Business in Nigeria, acknowledges and commends the ongoing engagements between the Federal Government and Organised Labour on the National Minimum Wage. We recognise the legitimate concerns regarding workers’ welfare, rising cost of living and declining purchasing power. “However, NECA strongly emphasises that the determination of the National Minimum Wage is fundamentally a Tripartite process that must involve Government, Employers and Workers as equal Social Partners. The broader principles of social dialogue are further reinforced by ILO Convention No. 144 and Recommendation No. 113. “The principle of Tripartism is firmly established in relevant International Labour Organisation (ILO) instruments, particularly the Minimum Wage Fixing Convention, 1970 (No. 131), Minimum Wage Fixing Recommendation, 1970 (No. 135), and Minimum Wage-Fixing Machinery Convention, 1928 (No. 26). These instruments underscore the importance of meaningful consultation and participation of the most representative employers’ body (NECA) and the most representative workers’ organisation (NLC) in minimum wage determination. “While NECA respects the right of Government and Organised Labour to hold bilateral discussions, such engagements cannot substitute for the statutory tripartite process. Organised private-sector employers cannot be deemed parties to, or contractually bound by, agreements reached without their participation and concurrence. This does not, however, diminish employers’ obligation to comply with any National Minimum Wage validly established under the National Minimum Wage Act. “For the avoidance of doubt, NECA is not opposed to the negotiation or review of the National Minimum Wage. Rather, the Association insists that the process must be inclusive, transparent, evidence-based and consistent with relevant ILO Conventions and Recommendations. A sustainable outcome must balance the legitimate needs of workers with the economic realities confronting employers.” The post N70,000 relief: Ajaero blasts TUC over rejection, as OPS sets condition for minimum wage appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Fuel spill nearly blinded me while working at Shell — Young Dee Group CEO
items.description: Young Dee Group Chief Executive Officer Desmond Darko has recounted a frightening accident during his days as a fuel attendant at Shell, when petrol splashed into his eyes, leaving him struggling to see. He said the incident occurred during a period of fuel shortages, when the station had to sell a full tanker load after it was discharged. Speaking on Joy FM’s Personality Profile with Lexis Bill on Thursday, October 29, Mr Darko said the pressure to sell the fuel meant he had to remain on his feet for long hours. Mr Darko, now owner of three fuel stations, explained that while taking pump readings, a trainee attendant who was assisting him accidentally splashed V-Power fuel into his face. “It entered my eyes. In fact, I had to wash my face for about 20 to 30 minutes before I was able to see well,” he said. Health risks Mr Darko said the accident exposed him to the risks associated with working around fuel, adding that prolonged exposure to petroleum products could also pose health challenges. He said he was advised to seek medical attention the following day and followed that advice. Looking back, he observed that workers in the filling station industry might not always appreciate the dangers they face, particularly when they lack adequate guidance on workplace safety and the need to seek prompt medical care after an accident. “Some of us didn’t actually know what we’re doing then,” he said, explaining that workers often concentrated on their duties without fully appreciating the potential consequences of exposure to hazardous substances. “We were just there working, working, working and here I am today,” he added. A lesson from experience Mr Darko’s account highlights the occupational risks that can accompany work at fuel stations, where employees routinely handle highly flammable petroleum products. His experience also underscores the importance of appropriate safety precautions and prompt medical attention following exposure to fuel. He said he was grateful to have come through the experience, reflecting on how little he and some of his colleagues understood about the health risks associated with their work at the time.

items.title: Omitted candidates: INEC upholds 41 of governorship petitions, rejects 28
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has upheld 41 of the 69 petitions filed against the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, while rejecting 28. Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC) of the commission, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday night. According to him, the petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states. He said, “The complaints concerned the omission of certain political parties, the wrongful inclusion of candidates of political parties whose names were not contained in the membership registers submitted by their political parties, and instances of alleged multiple nominations.” Haruna said the commission examined the complaints against its records and the law. “Following a review of the complaints, relevant records and applicable legal provisions, the Commission found merit in some representations and approved the inclusion of affected candidates and their political parties, while complaints found to be without merit were declined. “In addition, some names that were wrongfully published in the final list were removed after verifying that their names were not on the register. “The Commission also approved the removal of candidates whose nominations were found to be inconsistent with the applicable legal requirements,” the statement said. Although INEC did not name any candidate or state, a source had earlier revealed that the commission’s meeting on Thursday to review complaints from parties and candidates left out of the lists had cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections, subject to the outcome of pending court cases. The source also said the petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list, did not succeed. “Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP governorship candidate in Gombe State. “He did not succeed,” the source said when asked about Adebutu. On the State Houses of Assembly, the commission said the decisions affecting candidates sponsored by political parties “were informed by specific complaints received and determined in accordance with the law and the Commission’s established criteria.” For those elections, INEC received 61 petitions from 11 political parties across 11 states. Twenty-five succeeded, while 36 failed. The commission said the affected candidates, political parties and states “will be reflected in the updated list on the Commission’s website.” “Once again, the Commission assures the public of its commitment to transparency and the credibility of the electoral process,” the statement said. items.title: EPA engages stakeholders in Savannah Region on ban on Styrofoam products
items.description: The Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) has engaged stakeholders in the Savannah Region, on the impending ban on Styrofoam products in the country. The one-day stakeholders’ engagement, held at Damongo, was attended by food vendors, restaurant operators, traditional and religious leaders, students, amongst other stakeholders. Representatives of the Ghana Police Service, Ghana Tourism Authority, Ghana Health Service and the Department of Agriculture were also in attendance. The ban on styrofoam products in Ghana will take effect on January 01, 2027, as part of efforts to reduce the environmental and health risks associated with these products. Professor Nana Ama Browne Klutse, Chief Executive Officer of the EPA, at the engagement, ‎called on households, food vendors, schools, traders and businesses to begin moving away from the use of styrofoam takeaway containers to other healthier alternatives. She said early adoption of alternative materials such as traditional plantain leaves, as well as biodegradable packaging, reusable containers and other materials that could break down naturally and/or be recycled, would make the transition easier when enforcement began. ‎She urged the participants to take the message to their homes, workplaces, markets and communities, to ensure that residents understood the importance of the ban and the need to adopt sustainable practices. Mr Salisu Be-Awuribe, the Savannah Regional Minister, expressed the region’s commitment to enforcing the ban, saying the Savannah Regional Coordinating Council, the Municipal and District Assemblies and the law enforcement agencies at checkpoints would enforce the ban. He expressed concern about the growing use and improper disposal of styrofoam takeaway containers in communities across the region, saying discarded containers often littered streets and public spaces, choking gutters and obstructing fluid flows in drains, contributing to flooding and undermining efforts to maintain clean communities. He, however, observed that switching to alternative packaging could create financial challenges for food vendors and traders, saying the EPA’s Savannah Regional Office had been directed to engage affected groups and educate them on affordable alternatives. ‎Dr Abu Iddrisu, the Savannah Regional Director, EPA, urged residents to take responsibility for keeping their surroundings clean and support measures aimed at reducing waste and promoting responsible disposal practices. Meanwhile, as part of preparations for enforcement of the ban, there will be public education and clean-up campaigns in the region running from now through to December this year. ‎It will target food vendors, including chop bars and restaurants, and also engage hotels, guest houses, shops, plastic retailers, schools, lorry stations and other public spaces.

items.title: Titus Glover urges Ga chiefs to defend traders affected by La Pleasure Beach demolition
items.description: The National Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Titus Glover, has urged traditional authorities in the Greater Accra Region to intervene in the demolition of traders’ stalls at La Pleasure Beach, saying their silence on issues affecting their communities is worrying. He believes chiefs must defend their people’s interests, especially when government decisions or actions threaten their livelihoods. He has therefore urged Ga traditional leaders to engage President John Dramani Mahama and his appointees to seek answers over the exercise. National Security operatives carried out the demolitions on Friday, October 2, 2026, following a request from Labadi Beach Hotel, owned by the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT). Mr Glover argued that traditional leaders in other parts of the country would not remain silent over similar developments. He cited the Ashanti Region, where he said authorities would engage the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, before implementing decisions affecting communities. “The chiefs in Greater Accra must not be mute. They shouldn’t be wearing clothes and attending government functions and all that,” he said. He added that young people wanted to see their traditional leaders actively defending their interests rather than remaining on the sidelines when their livelihoods were threatened. “This is the time that we, the youth, want to see our chiefs speaking and defending us. They must speak to defend their people. You can’t do this in Ashanti Region. At least, you engage the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, [and explain] the reason why you want to do that,” he said. Mr Glover also expressed concern about what he described as the lack of a strong response from Ga traditional authorities, contrasting their silence with the level of engagement he believes exists between traditional leaders and authorities in other regions. “But we the Gas, look at how they are treating us,” he said, urging the chiefs to take a more visible role in matters affecting their communities. He made the appeal in an interview with Sammie Wiafe on Citi FM on Thursday, October 29, insisting that traditional leaders must speak out when their people’s welfare is at stake. “So I am really cautioning and appealing that they need to sit up and stand up. At least, when they speak, it goes far,” he added.

items.title: Youth in Amansie communities benefit from Asanko Gold Ghana Ltd apprenticeship programme
items.description: Youth from communities in the Amansie South and Amansie West districts are benefiting from a Community Skills and Apprenticeship Programme spearheaded by Asanko Gold Ghana Ltd. The beneficiaries, categorised under the first and second cohorts, have been engaged in training in areas including welding, electrical work, HME mechanics, health and safety, assay laboratory assistance, blast assistance, drilling offsider operations and heavy equipment operation. Among the beneficiaries are women operating heavy-duty trucks, welding and taking on technical roles. A total of 71 beneficiaries graduated after completing one year of training across the technical and operational fields. About 40 beneficiaries from Cohort One have gained full-time employment with Asanko and its business partners, while others have saved enough to return to school, with some moving on to pursue other opportunities. The hands-on training was assessed by the Ghana Technical and Vocational Institute, which accredited the trainers’ competency certificates. The company also facilitated Minerals Commission operator certification for the trainees. A total of 75 participants inducted into Cohort Two will undergo similar training, with the overall aim of equipping them to take up future job opportunities either within the company or elsewhere. Speaking during the graduation and induction ceremony at Manso Nkwanta, the General Manager of Asanko Gold Ghana Ltd, Justice Fenteng, urged beneficiaries from both cohorts to embrace the initiative and work towards improving themselves and their communities. He explained that the programme was designed to equip young people in host communities with employable skills, particularly in the mining industry. “This is a contribution to the community, so we can train our youth to be employable especially in our industry. Because we would like to have a lot of local employees, but if they don’t have the skills then it becomes difficult for us to pick them and we will have to fall on people in the region. And so having this training program which is not just sponsored by Asanko but also our business partners to give people opportunity to train in both technical and operational fields,” he said. The Coordinating Director for the Amansie West District, Okrah Thomas Kwame, lauded the initiative and urged the beneficiaries to take advantage of the programme to make an impact in their respective communities. The Sompahene, Nana Oppong Mensah Abrampah, who represented the Paramount Chief of the Manso Nkwanta Traditional Area, commended Asanko for the various programmes it continues to implement to promote development in the community. He called on residents to regard the company as a key development partner and help maintain a sound environment for its operations to facilitate the development of host communities. He also urged Asanko to increase the number of beneficiaries in future editions of the programme. One of the graduates from Cohort One, who was unemployed after completing university, said the programme had presented her with a greater opportunity than she had ever imagined. She said the programme had helped reduce unemployment in her community, Essuowin, as she had been employed following the training. She added that the opportunity would help transform her life and that of her family. The programme is being implemented by Asanko Gold Ghana Ltd and its business partners, including Drill Masters Africa, Rabotec Ghana Limited, Intertek Minerals, BLOJ Company Limited, Rocksure International, Solar Nitro and A. Kanin Limited.

items.title: Asanko screens over 300 residents, strengthens cancer awareness in host communities
items.description: Over 300 residents of Asanko Gold Ghana Ltd’s host communities received free health screening as part of the company’s Cancer Awareness Month activities. The program combined breast health education with breast and prostate cancer screening and broader medical checks under the theme “Early Detection Saves Lives.” Delivered with strong support from the Amansie South District Health Directorate’s medical team, the exercise included blood pressure monitoring, blood sugar checks, urine testing, body mass index assessments and full blood count tests. Free medication was administered to participants who needed it, while those requiring further assessment or treatment were referred to appropriate health facilities. A breast health education session covered warning signs, risk factors, screening and when to seek medical advice. It also addressed misconceptions that can delay care and provided guidance on supporting people affected by breast cancer. The Paramount Queen Mother of the Manso Nkwanta Traditional Area, Nana Nyarko Aboraa Sika III, who chaired the event, urged residents to make breast cancer awareness and appropriate health checks a year-round priority. She cautioned against waiting until October each year to revisit the subject, stressing that conversations about cancer and attention to personal health should continue beyond the awareness month. Reflecting on past community experiences, she said some deaths had been regarded as mysterious when the underlying illnesses had not been identified. She expressed concern about people waiting until they noticed a problem before seeking medical attention. Nana Nyarko Aboraa Sika III commended Asanko for the initiative. Drawing on the principle that prevention is better than cure, she welcomed the emphasis on early detection and timely care. She also thanked the company for the opportunity to chair an event addressing a subject important to her. Asanko’s General Manager, Justice Fenteng, explained that breast cancer remained the main focus of the company’s October awareness activities, with prostate cancer included to encourage men to take an active interest in their health. He urged residents to seek professional advice, understand their screening results and follow through on recommended care. Mr. Fenteng acknowledged that fear, uncertainty, transport difficulties, cost and competing work or family responsibilities could delay medical attention. He encouraged families and neighbours to offer practical support, including helping relatives attend follow-up appointments. He linked good health to the everyday responsibilities and ambitions of residents, from caring for children and tending farms to running businesses and pursuing education or employment. Supporting community wellbeing, he said, remained an important part of the company’s relationship with its host communities. The event was attended by the Acting District Health Director for Amansie South, Mr. Randy Osei-Boakye, traditional representatives and representatives of the District Health Directorate. The company’s awareness activities also extended to staff through education and screening services at the onsite clinic. Asanko’s Medical Team, led by Dr. Kwasi Safo, Unit Manager, Health Services, educated staff on breast and prostate cancer. Breast screening was provided at the clinic, while men in the eligible age group were encouraged to visit for prostate cancer screening. Dr. Safo also noted that the company had arranged mammogram appointments for all female staff above 40. Across the community and staff activities, participants received guidance on their results, everyday health practices and when to seek further medical attention. The program reinforced the importance of sustained awareness and completing recommended follow-up care beyond the screening day.

items.title: Mahama visits Kente Exhibition by Russia-Ghana Parliamentary Forum in Moscow
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama on Thursday visited the Kente Exhibition by the Russia-Ghana Parliamentary Forum as part of the official activities surrounding the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow. The Exhibition, which is being organised by the Russia-Ghana Parliamentary Forum in collaboration with the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA) and Ghana’s Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, seeks to showcase Ghana’s rich cultural heritage through kente, one of the country’s most iconic and internationally recognized traditional textiles. President Mahama, in his remarks, commended their friends from the Russian Parliamentary Group for their friendship with Ghana. “While we have contacts from government to government, and we have relations between our two governments, the more enduring partnerships are the relations between people and people,” he stated. “People-to-people relationships, and the only way we can consolidate people-to-people relationships is to understand each other’s cultures.” The President noted that he was very appreciative that the Ghana Export Promotion Authority, together with their partners, had been able to bring the Kente Exhibition to Moscow. “I understand, almost 11,000 people have so far come to see this exhibition, and it is well laid out, and all the explanations have been translated into Russian, and so you can understand the Adinkra symbols and all the exhibits that are here,” President Mahama said.

items.title: Mourir seul, loin de ses proches, une épreuve qui appelle notre solidarité
items.description: À l’approche de la Toussaint, ce dimanche 1er novembre, des milliers de Français se rendent dans les cimetières pour honorer leurs défunts. Des fleurs déposées sur une tombe, un regard posé sur une pierre, des souvenirs qui resurgissent : ces gestes rappellent une vérité profonde. Nous ne sommes pas faits pour oublier ceux que nous avons aimés. Mais que deviennent celles et ceux qui meurent sans personne à leurs côtés ? Sans une main à tenir, sans une voix familière pour les rassurer, sans un proche pour accompagner leurs derniers instants ? Mourir seul est déjà une épreuve douloureuse. Mais lorsque l’identité d’une personne demeure inconnue, que ses proches ne peuvent être retrouvés ou que ses dernières volontés ne sont pas connues, une difficulté supplémentaire apparaît : comment garantir le respect de sa dignité et de ses convictions jusque dans la mort ? Pour un musulman, cette situation peut également soulever la question de l’accomplissement des rites funéraires auxquels il était attaché. Cette réalité concerne notamment des personnes âgées, des personnes immigrées, des personnes malades ou des individus progressivement coupés de leurs proches. Derrière ces situations, il y a des vies, des parcours et des histoires que l’isolement ne devrait jamais effacer. Mohamed, 78 ans, et le risque de mourir dans la solitude Imaginons le cas de Mohamed, 78 ans, originaire de Batna, en Algérie, installé à Lyon depuis 1970. Un matin, alors qu’il sort acheter une baguette, il est percuté par une voiture. Transporté aux urgences, il meurt quelques heures plus tard. Sans document d’identité, son identité n’est pas immédiatement établie. Aucun proche ne se manifeste dans l’immédiat. Derrière cet homme, il y a pourtant toute une vie : une enfance, des souvenirs, des années de travail, des joies et des épreuves, entre la France et l’Algérie. Lorsqu’aucun proche ne peut être retrouvé ou mobilisé, les démarches nécessaires à l’organisation des obsèques peuvent devenir plus complexes. Sans informations sur l’identité, les convictions ou les volontés du défunt, il est plus difficile de s’assurer que ses souhaits seront pris en considération. Qui veillera à ce que sa dépouille soit traitée avec respect ? Qui pourra organiser la toilette rituelle, la prière funéraire et l’inhumation selon le rite musulman ? Qui s’assurera que ses volontés soient prises en considération ? La dignité ne s’arrête pas au dernier souffle Dans la tradition musulmane, la dignité du défunt demeure une responsabilité pleine et entière pour les vivants. La toilette mortuaire, le linceul, la prière funéraire et l’inhumation témoignent du respect dû à la personne, quelle que soit son origine ou sa situation sociale. L’absence de proches immédiats ne signifie pas pour autant que ces rites sont impossibles. Des mosquées, des associations et des professionnels peuvent y contribuer. Encore faut-il que les convictions du défunt soient connues et que les acteurs concernés puissent se coordonner. Accompagner un défunt, c’est reconnaître qu’une vie a compté. Mais cette responsabilité ne peut reposer uniquement sur la bonne volonté de quelques bénévoles. Elle exige une organisation et une mobilisation durables. Savons-nous repérer ceux qui ne fréquentent plus nos mosquées, qui vieillissent seuls, qui sont malades ou qui n’ont plus de contacts réguliers avec leurs proches ? Une communauté ne se mesure pas seulement à sa capacité de rassembler, mais aussi à l’attention qu’elle porte aux plus isolés. Transformer la solidarité en action Il est urgent de structurer notre action. Les mosquées et les associations musulmanes ont un rôle clé à jouer : renforcer les visites aux personnes isolées, désigner des référents pour les décès sans proches identifiés et nouer des partenariats pérennes avec les services sociaux, les établissements de santé, les collectivités et les professionnels du funéraire. Il est également essentiel d'informer les fidèles sur les démarches permettant de faire connaître leurs volontés funéraires de leur vivant. Une meilleure coordination entre les acteurs concernés faciliterait leur prise en compte et le respect des convictions de chacun. Ne laissons personne mourir dans l’oubli La Toussaint nous invite à nous souvenir de nos morts, mais elle doit aussi nous inciter à regarder celles et ceux qui risquent de quitter ce monde sans témoin ni famille à leurs côtés. Nous ne pouvons empêcher toutes les morts solitaires, mais nous pouvons agir pour que l’isolement ne condamne personne à l’oubli. Ne laissons pas nos frères et nos sœurs quitter ce monde dans l’anonymat, faute d’avoir su nous organiser pour eux. Faisons en sorte que leur dignité soit préservée et que la fraternité ne s’arrête pas au dernier souffle. Car aucune vie humaine ne perd sa valeur lorsqu’elle s’achève. Personne ne devrait être abandonné dans l’indifférence au moment de quitter ce monde. *Recteur de la mosquée de Villeurbanne L’article Mourir seul, loin de ses proches, une épreuve qui appelle notre solidarité est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 2027: INEC grants provisional clearance to Pantami, Gwarzo – Source
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi & Ben Ngwakwe There were strong indications on Thursday night that the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC might have provisionally cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The clearance of both men is subject to the outcome of pending court cases, it was learned on Thursday night. In Gombe, Pantami’s supporters took over some major areas celebrating the development on Thursday night. INEC officials did not immediately react to Vanguard’s questions regarding the development. But a source said the decisions were reached at the commission’s meeting on Thursday to consider complaints from political parties and candidates whose names were left out of the lists published ahead of the 2027 elections. The source added that the commission had no objection to their candidacies, but that the pending legal proceedings could still affect the final outcome. The development comes after INEC dropped Pantami’s name from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State, although he appeared on the provisional list published on August 29. Pantami emerged as the PDP candidate after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. One of the aspirants for the ticket, Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, challenged his victory in court. A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again. His biggest hurdle was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time. Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had previously said that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027. The commission, however, rejected a petition by the PDP governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, who had asked it to review his exclusion from the list of candidates. items.title: 3ᵉ Sommet Russie–Afrique à Moscou : Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré appelle à transformer le partenariat en réalisations concrètes
items.description: Intervenant ce jeudi 29 octobre 2026 à Moscou au nom du Chef de l'État, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le Premier ministre burkinabè Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo a livré un discours d'orientation majeur lors du panel de haut niveau marquant le deuxième jour du troisième Sommet Russie–Afrique. Plaçant cette rencontre sous le signe de l'action concrète après les jalons posés à Sotchi en 2019 et à Saint-Pétersbourg en 2023, Ouagadougou réclame un partenariat fondé sur la réciprocité, le transfert effectif de technologies de pointe et la formation de la jeunesse. Réaffirmant l'engagement commun des nations de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES) pour leur souveraineté et la reconquête territoriale, le message présidentiel appelle à une refonte de la gouvernance mondiale pour que l'Afrique cesse d'être perçue comme un simple réservoir de matières premières ou un champ d'affrontement géopolitique. Le troisième Sommet Russie–Afrique doit marquer le passage décisif de la parole aux actes. Prenant la parole au cours du panel de haut niveau réuni dans la capitale russe, le Chef du Gouvernement burkinabè, le Camarade Premier ministre Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a porté avec solennité la vision du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Pour les autorités de la Transition, ce rendez-vous moscovite ne saurait se borner à une réitération de principes généraux : il doit impérativement concrétiser les fondations posées à Sotchi en 2019 et consolidées à Saint-Pétersbourg en 2023, afin d'apporter des réponses tangibles aux attentes profondes des populations africaines. Au cœur de la vision burkinabè de la coopération se trouve le refus des tutelles paternalistes et des relations asymétriques. Sous le leadership du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le Burkina Faso prône un modèle reposant sur le respect mutuel, la réciprocité et un véritable transfert de savoir-faire. La formation des jeunes générations constitue le pilier central de cette ambition : Ouagadougou souhaite élargir les opportunités pour les étudiants burkinabè et africains d'accéder aux universités et instituts russes dans les domaines des technologies de pointe et des secteurs stratégiques, avec pour mission de réinvestir ces compétences au service du développement économique endogène. Cette quête d'autonomie s'enracine dans la volonté politique de maîtriser les ressources nationales et de choisir librement ses alliances internationales sur la base d'intérêts partagés. Ce combat pour l'émancipation s'articule étroitement avec les pays frères du Mali et du Niger au sein de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES). Dans son adresse, le Chef de l’État a salué la mémoire, la détermination et le sacrifice des forces combattantes qui luttent sur le théâtre des opérations contre le terrorisme, permettant ainsi la reconquête continue des localités, la réouverture des écoles et la réinstallation progressive des populations éprouvées. Le message a également convoqué les racines historiques qui unissent l’Afrique et la Russie, depuis le soutien apporté par l'Union soviétique aux jeunes nations africaines au lendemain des indépendances jusqu'à la formation de leurs premiers cadres. Cet attachement demeure particulièrement vivace au Burkina Faso, héritier de la Révolution d'août 1983 portée par le Président Thomas Sankara. Élargissant sa réflexion à la scène internationale, Ouagadougou a interpellé les puissances sur les déséquilibres de la gouvernance globale. Pointant les crises de légitimité et les défaillances des institutions internationales, le message du Chef de l'État a plaidé pour un respect effectif du droit international et une réforme structurelle des instances multilatérales. C'est dans ce cadre que résonne la formule la plus incisive de l'allocution présidentielle : « L’Afrique ne veut être ni un champ de bataille, ni un réservoir de matières premières, ni un vote dans une assemblée. Elle veut être une terre de dignité » . Pour le Burkina Faso, la valeur d'une alliance se juge ainsi à sa sincérité et à son équilibre, en offrant une coopération qui n’impose pas au continent de s’aligner sur un camp, mais qui lui donne les moyens de bâtir souverainement son propre avenir. L’article 3ᵉ Sommet Russie–Afrique à Moscou : Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré appelle à transformer le partenariat en réalisations concrètes est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: 18ᵉ édition du SIAO : La journée de travail continu instaurée dans le Kadiogo du 30 octobre au 8 novembre 2026
items.description: À l’occasion de la tenue de la 18ᵉ édition du Salon International de l’Artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), le Ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple a officialisé l'instauration de la journée de travail continu dans la province du Kadiogo. Couvrant la période du vendredi 30 octobre au dimanche 8 novembre 2026, cette mesure fixe les horaires de service de 07h30 à 14h00 pour l'ensemble des travailleurs et employeurs des secteurs public et privé. Conformément au décret présidentiel du 23 septembre 2026, un dispositif de service minimum demeure obligatoire dans les structures à activités continues afin de garantir la permanence des prestations essentielles. La capitale burkinabè adapte son rythme d'activité à l'heure du SIAO. À la veille du lancement de la 18ᵉ édition du Salon International de l’Artisanat de Ouagadougou, vitrine continentale de la créativité et des métiers d'art, le gouvernement a décidé d'ajuster l'organisation du travail. Par voie de communiqué officiel émanant du Secrétariat général du Ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple, les autorités ont annoncé l'application de la journée de travail continu sur l'ensemble de la province du Kadiogo pour toute la durée de la manifestation, soit du vendredi 30 octobre au dimanche 8 novembre 2026. Cette décision s'inscrit dans un cadre réglementaire précisément défini. Elle découle de l’application du décret n°2026-1067/PF/PRIM/MSP/MATM du 23 septembre 2026, qui régit les conditions et les modalités de déclaration de la journée de travail continu dans les administrations publiques et les entreprises privées au Burkina Faso. Ainsi, pendant cette dizaine de jours, la plage horaire quotidienne de travail est strictement arrêtée de 07 heures 30 minutes à 14 heures 00 minute, permettant de concilier obligations professionnelles et participation citoyenne à cet événement d'envergure nationale et internationale. La flexibilité accordée aux agents ne doit en aucun cas paralyser le fonctionnement des services indispensables. Le ministère a expressément rappelé que dans les secteurs à activités continues — tels que les structures sanitaires, la sécurité ou les services d'astreinte —, chaque entité est tenue de s’organiser en interne pour assurer le service minimum nécessaire. En facilitant les déplacements et l'accès aux pavillons d'exposition tout en préservant la continuité de l'action publique, l'État entend faire de ce 18ᵉ SIAO une réussite populaire et organisationnelle pleine et entière. L’article 18ᵉ édition du SIAO : La journée de travail continu instaurée dans le Kadiogo du 30 octobre au 8 novembre 2026 est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Mahama joins African leaders at Russia – Africa Forum in Moscow
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama on Wednesday joined fellow African leaders at the Russia –Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum in Moscow, where Russian President Vladimir Putin called for a fairer multipolar world order and greater representation of developing countries in global affairs. Addressing the plenary session, President Putin declared that the era of global decision-making dominated by a narrow bloc of countries was ending, with new centres of global governance emerging. “We are witnessing a Multipolar World truly becoming a reality, and this trend is objective and irreversible,” he said. President Putin said Russia was committed to deepening its economic and humanitarian relations with African countries, with the forum providing a platform for dialogue and cooperation on shared development priorities. He disclosed that Russia exported more than 13 million tonnes of agricultural produce to Africa between January and September 2026, underscoring the importance of agricultural trade in relations between Russia and the continent. President Putin said the forum’s commitment to “free and open dialogue” reflected the scale and depth of the ongoing transformation in global affairs. He said the emerging world order should ensure that the voices of all countries participating in international affairs were heard. Citing economic trends, President Putin said the BRICS countries had accounted for more than 40 per cent of global Gross Domestic Product (GDP) over the past five years, compared with less than 30 per cent for the Group of Seven (G7). He expressed confidence that the balance would continue to shift in favour of developing countries. President Putin said Africa was increasingly asserting itself as a major force in global economic and political affairs, with growing sovereignty and international influence. “The continent is experiencing a new awakening: its sovereignty is growing stronger, and its influence and standing on the world stage are increasing,” he said. He said Africans had an unwavering determination to defend their interests, shape their future and choose their own paths of development. Quoting the late Thomas Sankara, former President of Burkina Faso, President Putin criticised debt as a form of neo-colonialism. “Debt is neo-colonialism, in which colonizers have transformed themselves into ‘technical assistants’,” he quoted Sankara as saying. The two-day forum, which ends on Thursday, October 29, provides a platform for discussions on trade, energy, technology, peace and security, and sustainable development, as Russia and African countries explore ways to deepen economic and diplomatic relations.

items.title: Lagarde, el ‘búho’ que pilotó durante dos décadas las finanzas mundiales sin estar predestinada a ello
items.description: A Christine Lagarde (París, 70 años, de soltera Christine Madeleine Odette Lallouette) le gusta enviar mensajes con su atuendo. Elige cuidadosamente sus pañuelos (hay quien cree adivinar en ellos sus intenciones) y, en momentos especialmente delicados, comparece en la rueda de prensa del BCE con un broche característico: un búho. En un mundo, el de la política monetaria, habitualmente dividido entre halcones , banqueros con poca tolerancia por la inflación y gatillo fácil a la hora de subir tipos, y palomas , más sensibles al efecto del dinero caro sobre la economía, Lagarde se desmarcaba con esta otra ave. Seguir leyendo

items.title: De la cabina al Ministerio: ¿qué falló en Urda? “No tiene sentido que con más tráfico tengamos menos inversión y menos personal”
items.description: En este episodio de Hoy en EL PAÍS , Ana Fuentes conversa con un maquinista de mercancías, un antiguo trabajador de Renfe vinculado durante años a la alta velocidad y un exdirector de calidad de Adif, para intentar entender qué ocurrió en el choque de trenes de Urda. Los tres repasan cómo funcionan las comunicaciones entre maquinistas y centros de control, el papel de los sistemas de seguridad y los cambios que ha vivido la red ferroviaria en las últimas décadas. ¿Qué ocurrió en los minutos previos al choque? ¿Por qué los profesionales del sector consideran tan excepcional este accidente? ¿Qué cambios creen necesarios para evitar que vuelva a repetirse? Seguir leyendo

items.title: Africa must help shape AI revolution transformation — Mahama
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has urged African nations to actively shape the global artificial intelligence (AI) revolution, calling for practical cooperation with Russia to ensure the continent benefits from the transformative technology. He made the appeal in his remarks at the Third Russia-Africa Forum in Moscow, hosted by Russian President Vladimir Putin. President Mahama emphasised that AI was fundamentally altering the global landscape. “Artificial Intelligence is changing how economies produce, how governments serve, and how people learn,” he stated. “Africa must help shape this transformation and develop the skills and infrastructures needed to benefit from it.” He outlined specific areas where Ghana was seeking practical cooperation on AI, including agriculture, healthcare, education, municipal services, transport management, tax and revenue collection, and environmental monitoring. To operationalise this vision, President Mahama proposed a new collaboration framework. “Ghana is prepared to explore a Russia-Africa digital innovation and Artificial Intelligence Programme that will bring together African universities, research institutions, businesses, and public agencies,” he announced. He explained that such a programme could support joint research, carefully assess pilot projects, and drive skills development across the continent. The proposal signals Ghana’s intent to position itself as a hub for AI innovation and a bridge between African expertise and Russian technological capabilities, aiming to harness AI for sustainable development and improved public service delivery.

items.title: Un año con Alcalá Norte: un grupo disfuncional ante el reto de su segundo disco
items.description: Hoy no parece un buen día para quedar con Alcalá Norte. Carlos Elías, el guitarrista, pasó una noche regular, aquejado de una incómoda infección de garganta. Álvaro Rivas , cantante, apenas pegó ojo y vomitó ocasionalmente. “Algo me debió sentar mal”, aduce. De Jaime Barbosa (batería) y Pablo Prieto (bajista) poco se sabe, y no asomarán la cabeza en toda la mañana. La única que se presenta despejada es Laura de Diego, la teclista. Pero se le tuerce el gesto a los pocos minutos de entrar en el estudio madrileño donde se graba el nuevo disco del grupo. Rivas habla sobre el pudor que le da escribir canciones con estribillos proclives a que la audiencia desate sus gargantas, como si eso fuera algo sencillo. “El otro día me comentó Jota [líder de Los Planetas] que siempre seremos un grupo de nicho, y creo que tiene razón”, apunta el cantante, quizá para reforzar la idea de huir de las composiciones facilonas. Laura interviene, con tono severo: “Harías mejor en no hacerle mucho caso a Jota”. Estamos en noviembre de 2025, un año antes de la publicación del segundo álbum de Alcalá Norte. Y no va a ser un camino sencillo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ghana has begun discussions with Rosatom on first nuclear power station – Mahama
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has announced that Ghana has begun discussions with the Russian State Nuclear Energy Corporation, Rosatom, to establish the country’s first nuclear power station. Speaking at the Third Russia-Africa Forum in Moscow, President Mahama highlighted the critical role of reliable electricity in Africa’s development. The President identified inadequate electricity as a major obstacle to Africa’s progress, stressing that industrialisation requires reliable, affordable energy to succeed. “We have initiated discussions with Rosatom on the establishment of Ghana’s first nuclear power station,” adding that Russia has a comparative advantage in renewable energy and nuclear power, an area where cooperation between Russia and Africa could yield tangible results. He noted that Ghana had a historical relationship with Russia in the peaceful use of nuclear energy, recalling that as far back as 1964, the Soviet Union provided Ghana with a two-megawatt nuclear reactor for scientific and research purposes. President Mahama stated that several Ghanaian nuclear scientists were trained in Russia to operate the reactor. The announcement marks a significant step in Ghana’s long-standing ambition to add nuclear power to its energy mix, as electricity demand grows with industrial expansion and population growth. A nuclear power station would provide baseload capacity to complement the country’s existing hydropower and thermal generation sources. President Mahama’s remarks underscore the broader case for strengthened Russia-Africa cooperation in the energy sector, with Moscow positioned as a partner in both renewable energy and nuclear technology. The President said such cooperation could deliver concrete results for the continent’s industrialisation drive.
