items.title: Los controladores de Atocha ordenaron seguir el protocolo equivocado antes del choque entre el AVE y el Iryo: “Me estaba liando”
items.description: Los controladores del centro de coordinación de Atocha (Madrid) ordenaron al AVE 2080 que siguiera un protocolo equivocado antes de que el miércoles embistiera al Iryo 6076 en la localidad toledana de Urda, causando al menos 69 muertos y 58 heridos. Así se desprende del libro de normas del maquinista de Renfe y de los testimonios recabados por este diario de tres expertos con experiencia en el manejo de la línea de alta velocidad que une Madrid y Sevilla. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Centro de Control de Atocha, un centenar de operarios entre la presión del tráfico y un ‘software’ de vanguardia
items.description: Falta de personal y una fuerte presión sobre los hombros de los operarios en horas pico de tráfico. Son dos de las quejas recurrentes de los sindicatos al referirse al Puesto de Mando y Centro de Regulación y Control (CRC) que el gestor de la infraestructura ferroviaria Adif tiene junto a la estación madrileña de Atocha. En él trabajan un centenar de personas en torno a Da Vinci, uno de los sistemas de vigilancia de la red ferroviaria más avanzados de Europa. Desde sus pantallas se monitoriza el control de tráfico centralizado, las comunicaciones fijas y GSMR, la señalización, sistemas de seguridad, sistemas de planificación y regulación del tráfico, videovigilancia y control de las estaciones. Hasta ahora, un motivo de orgullo para la compañía dependiente del Ministerio de Transportes, pero es aquí donde se fragua la cadena de órdenes inconexas que acaban el miércoles en tragedia , con el choque de dos trenes y al menos 69 víctimas, en la localidad toledana de Urda. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Preguntas y respuestas sobre el accidente de Urda: lo que explican y lo que no los audios entre los maquinistas y el centro de control
items.description: Los audios de las conversaciones entre el centro de mando de la estación de Atocha y los maquinistas de los trenes siniestrados este miércoles cerca de Urda (Toledo), apuntan, como había señalado desde el primer momento el Ministerio de Transportes, a un error humano. Pero un análisis pormenorizado con expertos, entre ellos, maquinistas, de esas grabaciones y la compleja jerga de siglas y acrónimos que manejan, hablan de un fallo mucho más extendido, que alude directamente al sistema. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Antonio despertó entre los hierros del tren e intentó proteger a su mujer: “Quería cubrirla con mis brazos, pero no podía moverlos”
items.description: El viaje a Sevilla era un regalo de sus hijas. Aquella mañana, Antonio Chao y Toñi Barba, ambos de 59 años, se despidieron de una de ellas antes de subir al AVE que los llevaría a pasar un par de días en la capital andaluza. Ella los había acercado en coche hasta la estación de Atocha. En el coche 7 tenían asignados los asientos 9B y 9A, uno junto al otro. Antonio recuerda con precisión los instantes previos al accidente. Lo que vino después se le aparece entre imágenes confusas que empiezan con un golpe seco, siguen con el vagón precipitándose por un terraplén y continúan cuando consigue abrir los ojos. Lo primero que hace entonces es buscar a su mujer. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sánchez mantiene el apoyo a Puente pese a la creciente presión contra él
items.description: La presión es enorme y va a crecer mucho en cuanto acabe el duelo oficial por los muertos en el accidente de Urda . Todo indica que la petición de dimisión de Óscar Puente, ministro de Transportes, será uno de los ejes de la campaña de PP y Vox en las próximas semanas. Pero no solo ellos apuntan a uno de los hombres clave del sanchismo, decisivo en la campaña socialista. También algunos socios importantes del PSOE, como el PNV o el Frente Amplio, están apuntando a su responsabilidad y rechazando la idea de que el accidente pueda explicarse simplemente con el argumento del “fallo humano” . Seguir leyendo

items.title: El PP respetará el luto, pero después apuntará a Sánchez: “Con la dimisión de Puente no basta”
items.description: Algunos dirigentes de la cúpula del Partido Popular no podían contener las lágrimas tras la confirmación este jueves, 30 horas después del accidente, de que la exministra Fátima Báñez era una de las víctimas mortales de la tragedia ferroviaria de Urda. La familia de la exdirigente del PP tuvo que afrontar una espera agónica hasta que los bomberos consiguieron recuperar su cuerpo de los restos de los vagones siniestrados, lo que retrasó su identificación y añadió todavía más impacto emocional a la noticia de su muerte entre sus allegados en el PP, que eran muchos. Báñez era una figura muy querida en el partido y su pérdida ha provocado una conmoción en el PP que explica también el tono contenido ante la catástrofe, según transmiten en la cúpula, pese a la furia que recorre a las filas populares contra el Gobierno. Génova ya había decidido, en todo caso, respetar el luto oficial y Alberto Núñez Feijóo se mantuvo este jueves, un día después del accidente, en un perfil institucional sin pedir dimisiones, aunque sí reclamó que se asuman responsabilidades políticas antes de la investigación. En el PP los ánimos están muy caldeados y la reflexión interna es que, superado el luto, se apuntará a Sánchez. “Con la dimisión de Puente no basta”, advierte un dirigente. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La tragedia golpea la maltrecha reputación del sistema ferroviario, ya castigada por Adamuz
items.description: En su primera comparecencia tras el accidente , el miércoles desde el puesto de mando de Urda (Toledo), el cariacontecido presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, se mostró consciente de que, además del coste en muertes y heridos y familias desoladas, la tragedia dejaría un legado más, uno en forma de destrozo en el crédito popular del ferrocarril. El Gobierno reforzará la seguridad para “reconstruir la confianza en nuestro sistema ferroviario de alta velocidad”, se comprometió el jefe del Ejecutivo. Para conseguirlo, hay tarea por delante, que las urnas dirán el 29-N a quién le toca asumir. Porque la catástrofe de Urda golpea una imagen, la del servicio de trenes en España, que ya está seriamente dañada, según muestran los datos demoscópicos disponibles. Seguir leyendo

items.title: 28 de octubre
items.description: Todo se quedó antiguo de repente: la visita al cardiólogo, la revisión de la caldera de gas, la cita con la fisio o el podólogo. Se quedó antigua la partida de cartas de los miércoles, la comida familiar de los jueves, el vermut con los amigos de los viernes y hasta el texto que tenía uno preparado para esta esquina del periódico se quedó de súbito obsoleto. Al principio, cuando apenas sabíamos, las cosas se iban quedando antiguas muy despacio, pero después de los primeros muertos la vida entera se quedó de golpe suspendida, antigua, igual que el tráfico rodado y los semáforos y el mobiliario urbano. La tarta de cumpleaños que tenías que recoger también se quedó antigua, se infartó, lo mismo que el siglo XXI. En los hospitales, los niños nos nacían antiguos y velábamos en los tanatorios cadáveres pretéritos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Morir por el color de la piel en la Francia de 2026
items.description: “Podría haber sido cualquiera de nosotros”. La frase se repite en bucle estos días entre los vecinos de Trappes tras el atentado racista en Francia, que dejó heridas a cinco personas, entre ellas una niña de 12 años, y se cobró la vida de Pengo Bossio Wangi, un hombre de 26 años. Algunos ya no salen de casa por miedo. Otros se sobresaltan cada vez que un vehículo pasa cerca. Casi todos sienten que llevan una diana en la espalda por el simple hecho de ser de origen africano o magrebí. Mientras lloran la pérdida de Bossio Wangi, un joven deportista muy querido en esta ciudad multicultural de la periferia de París —donde crecieron, entre otros, el actor Omar Sy o el futbolista Nicolas Anelka ―, los vecinos se preguntan: ¿cuánto odio tiene que albergar una persona para disparar ocho veces a una niña solo por el color de su piel? La hipervigilancia como secuela del atentado los tiene agotados. Pero sobre todo sienten rabia contra quienes dan altavoz al odio en prime time , un día tras otro: medios de extrema derecha como CNews y canales de información continua de corte sensacionalista como LCI o BFM, cuyos platós se han convertido en escenarios de banalización de las ideas racistas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los hijos de Warren Buffett y el marrón de heredar 150.000 millones de dólares: “Nadie debería disponer de tanto dinero, no es natural”
items.description: Las puertas se cierran con un chasquido. Una luz estroboscópica parpadea y allí, en una nube de humo teatral, aparece un tren. La risa desquiciada del cantante de heavy metal Ozzy Osbourne inunda el almacén mientras Crazy Train retumba por los altavoces. Howard Buffett sí que sabe cómo hacer una entrada triunfal. El hijo mediano de Warren Buffett es quien ha conjurado este sueño delirante en Decatur, la pequeña ciudad de Illinois donde vive. Este decorado bizarro es una muestra de una de sus pasiones personales: un centro de formación policial que ha construido aquí con fondos benéficos de su padre, el Oráculo de Omaha. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La inevitable (o insoportable) levedad de los políticos en Madrid, donde solo Ayuso permanece
items.description: Isabel Díaz Ayuso quiere lanzar una especie de maldición. Es una decisión premeditada. Fría. Mira a Manuela Bergerot, la portavoz de Más Madrid en la Asamblea regional, que no encabezará la lista electoral de su partido en las próximas elecciones. Luego, a Mar Espinar, su homóloga del PSOE, en la misma situación. Y lanza su profecía : “Este, desde luego, es el último debate de toda su vida política como portavoces”. Son las palabras de una superviviente que ha visto caer a casi todos sus rivales. Solo la presidenta regional ha conseguido cabalgar la silla eléctrica de la política madrileña —siempre entrecruzada con la nacional— desde que accedió al poder por primera vez, allá por agosto de 2019. La lista de caídos, a la que se acaba de sumar el delegado del Gobierno, Francisco Martín , dimitido por no entrar en las listas electorales socialistas para las generales, es larga y multifactorial. Hay políticos de PSOE, Más Madrid, Podemos, Vox o Cs. Y también del propio PP. A la espera de las elecciones autonómicas de 2027, lo único seguro es que en el Madrid de Ayuso, por ahora, solo resiste la propia Ayuso. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Coalition condemns alleged sexual misconduct at Obuasi SHTS, calls for urgent action
items.description: The Coalition of Parents of Students in Private Institutions (COPOSIPI) has expressed grave concern over allegations of sexual misconduct involving Abdulai Zakaria, the Headmaster of Obuasi Senior High/Technical School (SHTS). The Coalition is therefore calling for urgent, impartial investigations and appropriate action in accordance with the law. In a statement signed by Dr Simon Gbene, the Executive Secretary of COPOSIPI, and copied to the Ghana News Agency, the statement said the safety, dignity, and welfare of every student, particularly girls, must be non-negotiable. It said any teacher or school administrator found to have engaged in sexual abuse or exploitation of students must face the full consequences of the law, stressing that such conduct had no place in Ghana’s educational institutions. They, therefore, called on the Ghana Education Service (GES) to take immediate steps to protect students, ensure due process, and strengthen safeguarding measures in both public and private schools. The group further urged the GES to conduct a comprehensive audit of schools to identify safeguarding gaps, investigate credible allegations of abuse, and remove individuals found guilty of such misconduct from positions where they could endanger children. The statement said, “COPOSIPI is prepared to pursue all lawful avenues, including seeking a mandamus order from the appropriate court, where legally justified, to compel the relevant authorities to discharge their statutory responsibilities in protecting students.” “To our girls and all students across the country, we want to assure you that your safety matters,” it said. It added that COPOSIPI would continue to advocate safe learning environments where every student could pursue an education free from abuse, intimidation, and exploitation. “Our children are not bargaining chips. Our schools must be places of learning, protection, and hope, not fear and exploitation,” it indicated. The statement encouraged students and parents to report suspected abuse through safe, appropriate channels.

items.title: Las llamadas entre Atocha y los maquinistas antes del choque de Urda, explicadas frase a frase
items.description: Pocas horas después del accidente de Urda se han difundido tres audios : uno recoge la conversación entre el Centro de Regulación de Circulación (CRC) de Adif, ubicado en Atocha, y el maquinista del tren AVE 02080. Era Antonio Acedo Meneses, que falleció en el choque . Las otras dos grabaciones son llamadas entre ese mismo centro y la maquinista del Iryo. No fueron las únicas: el puesto de mando de Atocha presumiblemente contactó con todos los trenes afectados por el fallo que pararía a los accidentados. Seguir leyendo Fuentes Las principales fuentes de normativa utilizadas para analizar los audios han sido el Reglamento de Circulación Ferroviaria (RD 664/2015) , texto consolidado del BOE, y los modelos oficiales de telefonema del LZB que incluye; el Libro de Normas del Maquinista, Grupo Renfe; Libro de Telefonemas Adif. En la realización de esta información se han utilizado agentes de inteligencia artificial para calcular las velocidades de los trenes y su posición aproximada. Los datos de geolocalización de trenes de Renfe proceden de los datos que publica la operadora en tiempo real y su histórico ha sido recopilado por la página web Retrasómetro, que utiliza datos públicos GTFS de Renfe.

items.title: Contrôles routiers au Burkina Faso : Le Ministère de la Sécurité met en garde contre les dérives autour de la carte « Laabal »
items.description: Dans un communiqué officiel rendu public ce jeudi 29 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, le Ministère de la Sécurité a fermement rappelé à l'ordre les agents chargés des contrôles routiers quant à l'usage de la carte « Laabal ». Destiné initialement à éviter la mise en fourrière systématique des engins, à accorder des facilités de paiement des amendes et à endiguer la corruption, ce dispositif ferait l'objet de détournements assimilables à du racket selon de nombreux témoignages d'usagers. Face à ces dérives contraires aux valeurs de probité prônées par la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP), le ministre invite les conducteurs en infraction à exiger systématiquement cette carte — une démarche désormais érigée en acte citoyen — tout en appelant au respect mutuel entre les forces de l'ordre et la population. Le dispositif conçu pour assainir les voies publiques et moderniser la gestion des contraventions se heurte à des résistances sur le terrain. Dans un communiqué officiel daté du 29 octobre 2026, le cabinet du Ministre de la Sécurité tire la sonnette d'alarme. Depuis l’instauration de la carte « Laabal » dans le protocole de paiement des amendes pour infractions au code de la route, de récurrents retours de citoyens font état de pratiques déviantes. Certains agents préposés aux contrôles routiers sont en effet accusés de détourner cet instrument de sa vocation première pour en faire un moyen de chantage ou de pression sur les automobilistes et motocyclistes, à des fins de concussion et de racket. Face à ces manquements jugés contraires aux principes d’intégrité, de probité et de justice sociale portés par la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP), l'autorité ministérielle a tenu à repréciser le cadre légal du mécanisme. La carte « Laabal » a été conçue pour offrir une alternative moderne et humaine aux usagers de la route : elle vise expressément à éviter la saisie systématique des véhicules et des deux-roues en permettant aux contrevenants de s'acquitter de leur amende à une date de leur convenance, coupant ainsi court aux arrangements illicites en espèces sur le bord des chaussées. Le ministère insiste sur le fait qu'il s'agit d'un outil de facilitation au bénéfice des contrevenants, et non d’une arme coercitive, rappelant à ce titre que l’exécution de travaux d’intérêt commun ne saurait constituer sa finalité première. Pour rétablir l'équilibre et protéger les droits des usagers, le gouvernement en appelle désormais à la vigilance active de la population. Le Ministre de la Sécurité invite formellement tout conducteur en infraction à exiger la délivrance de la carte « Laabal », précisant que ce réflexe sera désormais reconnu comme un véritable acte citoyen susceptible de constituer une circonstance atténuante. Rappelant avec force que la chaussée doit demeurer un espace de civisme partagé où agents de sécurité et usagers se doivent courtoisie et transparence, le ministre a conclu son message en saluant le dévouement et le professionnalisme de la majorité des Forces de Défense et de Sécurité (FDS) engagées au quotidien pour la sûreté de la nation. L’article Contrôles routiers au Burkina Faso : Le Ministère de la Sécurité met en garde contre les dérives autour de la carte « Laabal » est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: From Shell attendant to business owner: The encounter that changed the life of Young Dee Group CEO Desmond Darko
items.description: A chance encounter at a Shell filling station set Desmond Darko, now the CEO of Young Dee Group, on a path he had never imagined for himself — owning a filling station. Mr Darko, now owner of three fuel stations, said a conversation with Kevin Okyere, Chief Executive Officer of Springfield Group, helped him recognise his potential and consider venturing into business independently. Until then, he had been content working at Shell, with no immediate plans to establish his own filling station. Speaking on Joy FM’s Personality Profile with Lexis Bill on Thursday, October 29, Mr Darko recounted how Mr Okyere approached him after he had served him at the Airport Shell station. “He asked me, ‘Don’t you think that you have what it takes to own a filling station by yourself?’” he recalled. Mr Darko said the question caught him by surprise, as business ownership was not something he had seriously considered at the time. “He said, ‘Yes, I think you can own one. So, whenever you need help, just let me know,’” he recounted. The brief exchange, he said, stayed with him and eventually changed how he viewed his future. From employee to entrepreneur Mr Darko said Mr Okyere’s confidence in him encouraged him to begin exploring the possibility of running his own filling station. He started working on the registration of his company and approached Shell to express interest in taking over a station whenever one became available. He said his experience working at Airport Shell had helped him develop the skills and reputation needed to pursue the opportunity. His responsibilities had also extended beyond a single station. According to him, Shell had deployed him to about three or four other stations to help revive their operations. That experience, he said, gave the company an opportunity to observe his capabilities and strengthened his confidence in pursuing his own venture. Mr Darko said he had not initially recognised business ownership as a realistic ambition until Mr Okyere drew his attention to the possibility. ‘He was my destiny changer’ Reflecting on the encounter, Mr Darko described Mr Okyere as someone who helped him recognise abilities he had not fully appreciated. “He was actually my destiny changer or something,” he said. He said the businessman had been someone he did not previously know, yet he offered encouragement and made himself available to help when needed. For Mr Darko, the encounter illustrated how a few words of confidence from another person could prompt someone to reconsider their ambitions and take steps towards a different future. He credited Mr Okyere with helping him identify his potential at a time when he was focused on his work rather than building a business of his own.

items.title: ‘The price at which product was imported is locked in’ – NPA explains LPG pricing
items.description: Ghana’s monthly LPG import arrangements are cushioning consumers against sharp price increases, the National Petroleum Authority (NPA) has explained. Abass Tasunti, Director of Economic Regulation and Planning at the NPA, said the tender programme fixes import prices for a month. This means local LPG prices can fall even as international market prices rise. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, he explained that each cargo typically covers a month’s supply. “And so, the price at which the product was imported is locked in for that one-month period.” That arrangement, he said, explains why LPG prices are dropping despite a significant increase in the next pricing window. “So, if you look at the next window, for example, the price of LPG is going up significantly, but we’ve seen LPG dropping instead of it going up, and that’s because we’ve already locked in the price at which we imported the LPG from the previous window, which was lower than the current prices.” The protection, however, depends on the price secured for each cargo. A new monthly consignment bought at a higher price can push local prices up. Mr Tasunti said this explained the previous sharp increase in LPG prices. The price changed after the month-long arrangement ended. The replacement supply cost more than the product used to set prices the previous month. The same system is now offering relief. Ghana had already secured its imported LPG at a lower price before the latest increase. “But going to this window, for example, we have been shielded again, shielded again from a sharp increase for the next window because we’ve already locked in the price at which the product was brought in, so that helps.” Mr Tasunti also explained why diesel faces different pressures. He said disruptions to major supply sources reduce the volume available on the market and drive prices up. He pointed to the Russia-Ukraine war and attacks on Russian refineries as factors affecting diesel supplies. “So sometimes when the major supply sources are shut or are closed, we don’t have enough products on the market, and so it will cause, of course, economics comes in supply and demand factors.” For LPG consumers, the immediate cushion comes from the import price already secured. The next monthly cargo can change that position, depending on how its purchase price compares with the previous supply.

items.title: Nuclear jingoism
items.description: INDIA’S nuclear jingoism was on ample display during Operation Marka-i-Haq in May 2025 when it fired dual-use BrahMos cruise missiles with conventional payload, unmindful of the fact that the dangerous caper could have been misconstrued by Pakistani air defenders as a nuclear attack. Despite an agreement on pre-notification of flight testing of ballistic missiles, the Indians, while testing the Agni V MIRV-capable missile, have shown a blithe disregard for established pre-notification protocols that mandate a 72-hour pre-test notification, a fact pointed out by Pakistan’s Foreign Office in 2024. While the Indians keep up an implacable momentum of vertical proliferation of nuclear and missile technology, the world indulges them through exceptionalism enshrined in the nuclear waiver for the Nuclear Suppliers Group and membership of the Missile Technology Control Regime. The Indians have slyly wangled the concession from the USA and IAEA in the civil nuclear deal to keep eight reactors out of IAEA oversight. These pressurised heavy water reactors consume less nuclear fuel than they produce, which can be harvested for strategic military purposes. It should be remembered that it was the Indians who introduced the nuclear arms race in the subcontinent because of their grandiose big-power pretensions. Their nuclear explosions in 1974 and 1998 forced Pakistan to follow suit out of its security compulsions. The world indulges India through nuclear exceptionalism. The Indian nuclear security architecture was provided conceptual ballast by Gen K. Sunderji and Krishna Subramanyam in the 1980s, when they came up with the notion of no-first use of nuclear weapons against a non-nuclear nation, with a caveat of making an exception for biological and chemical attacks. However, India kept developing its conventional forces, especially the armoured and mechanised component, as per the Sunderji doctrine, aimed at tearing Pakistan asunder. On the geopolitical level the Indians have acquiesced to the status of a regional surrogate to accommodate balancing needs of the US vis-a-vis a rising global competitor, China. While enjoying nuclear exceptionalism the Indians went on a shopping spree for nuclear technology as well as the conventional hardware to operationalise the military strategy that sought an elusive space for conventional wars under the nuclear overhang. The operational manifestation of these military ambitions was a slew of concepts starting with Cold Start and graduating to proactive operations. The latest manifestation of those concepts is the Dynamic Response Strategy that is based on rapidly deployable all-arms-based integrated battle groups and multidomain-enabled terrain-customised brigade-sized groups called Rudra Brigades. Pakistan relies on its full-spectrum deterrence, keeping strategic nuclear ambiguity for greater liberty of action to deny India the space for conventional conflict. While India deploys non-state actors to keep Pakistan destabilised through terrorism, it cleverly conflates Pakistan’s principled support to the victims of Indian state repression in Occupied Kashmir, a UNSC-recognised dispute, with militancy. It has also withdrawn from its international law commitments by illegally holding the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance and imperilling the food security of Pakistan. India under the BJP and RSS sway has adopted a foreign policy based upon the antiquated notion of ‘Akhand Bharat’ that covets the territories of neighbours based on historical myths. The inflammatory statement of Prime Mi­­ni­s­ter Narendra Modi at Bar­m­­er, Rajasthan, during an el­­e­ction rally that “Indian nukes are not kept for Diwali” in­­dicates a bellicose mi­­­ndset. It is against the backdrop of the above facts that the notions of nuclear deterrence in the subcontinent have to be understood. Since the stability of nuclear deterrence is based upon nuclear dialectics between two rational actors, Indian irrationality adds dangerous instability to the nuclear equation. The deployment of canisterised ground-based ready-to-use nuclear missiles and the submarine-launched nuclear ballistic missiles point to an aggressive nuclear intent when viewed in the context of Indo-Pak distrust and irrationality of the ideologically driven BJP leadership. The well-known military historian Martin Van Creveld had coined a term for wars in the nuclear era: “Non-trinitarian”, where, unlike Clausewitz’s trinitarian wars, the only political objective would be deterring and not winning the wars. Whether India has strengthened or reduced its strategic deterrence by fielding shallow-range submarine-based missiles is a point to ponder by Indian nuclear strategists. The writer is a PhD from NUST. rwjanj@hotmail.com Published in Dawn, October 30th, 2026

items.title: Dédougou : « Les mauvais esprits » le poussent à l’évasion
items.description: Condamné en 2023 pour 11 ans de prison ferme dont huit ans de sureté avec 500 000 F CFA d’amende pour des faits de grand banditisme, D.K, courant juin 2026, a tenté de se défaire de son incarcération. Entre temps, la commission d’application des peines lui a donné une chance. Il a bénéficié d’une commutation de peine. Pour ce faire, il a été placé sur l’un des sites du domaine pénitencier de Dédougou pour l’exécution des Travaux d’intérêt général (TIG). Avec cette faveur qui lui a été faite, il devrait être libéré en 2028. Mais le prévenu a dit trouver ce temps un peu long. Il a comparu en audience correctionnelle devant le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Dédougou, le mardi 27 octobre 2026, pour répondre de ces faits de tentative d’évasion. Sans détour le prévenu a reconnu les faits. Pour sa défense, il a avancé être poussé par ‘’des mauvais esprits’’ à s’échapper du domaine pénitencier. C’est de concert avec un certain E.Z, un militaire radié selon le procureur du Faso, que le prévenu a mis en route son plan d’évasion. Il a pris le téléphone d’une tierce personne à l’aide duquel, il a envoyé un message vocal à sa copine pour lui faire part de son projet de s’évader de son lieu de placement vers un pays étranger et demander à cette dernière de le rejoindre dès qu’il va réussir son opération. Mais c’était sans compter avec la vigilance des Gardes de sécurité pénitentiaire (GSP). Son projet est déjoué. Mais avant cette tentative d’évasion, D.K. avait, courant décembre 2023, tenté une première évasion. Saisi d’une lettre de dénonciation du juge d’application des peines, le parquet a expliqué avoir entrepris de faire comparaître le mis en cause. D’après le ministère public, aucune faveur ne devrait être accordée à D.K. parce qu’il en avait déjà bénéficié. Après avoir affirmé que les faits reprochés au prévenu sont bien caractérisés, il a requis contre lui une peine de prison de 24 mois et une amende de 600 000 FCFA, le tout ferme. Malgré la demande de pardon de D.K, le tribunal l’a reconnu coupable avant d’entériner les réquisitions du parquet. Les juges ont précisé que cette peine est cumulative avec celle que le prévenu purgeait déjà. Outre cela, ils ont fixé la contrainte judiciaire à trois mois et décerné un mandat de dépôt contre lui. Source : Sidwaya.info L’article Dédougou : « Les mauvais esprits » le poussent à l'évasion est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: S&P Global Ratings attribue à la Commune de Casablanca la notation "BBB-/A-3", assortie d’une perspective stable
items.description: La Commune de Casablanca a annoncé l’attribution, par l’agence internationale de notation financière S&P Global Ratings, d’une notation de crédit de « BBB- » à long terme et « A-3 » à court terme, assortie d’une perspective stable. Cette notation constitue une reconnaissance de la solidité de la gestion financière de la Commune, de la résilience de ses performances budgétaires et de sa capacité à mobiliser des ressources diversifiées pour accompagner le développement de la métropole, indique la Commune dans un communiqué. Dans son rapport publié le 22 octobre 2026, S&P Global Ratings souligne les perspectives favorables de la situation financière de la Commune, portées notamment par la progression des recettes, le renforcement du recouvrement fiscal et la maîtrise des dépenses de fonctionnement. L’agence prévoit une amélioration progressive de l’épargne brute, qui devrait atteindre environ 25 % des recettes de fonctionnement à l’horizon 2028, contre 19 % en 2025, rapporte le communiqué, notant que cette évolution devrait permettre à la Commune de financer une part croissante de ses investissements à partir de ses ressources propres, tout en limitant le recours à de nouveaux emprunts. Le rapport met également en évidence les efforts engagés en matière de modernisation et de digitalisation de l’administration fiscale, d’élargissement de l’assiette fiscale et d’amélioration de l’efficacité du recouvrement des recettes communales. La notation tient compte du rôle stratégique de Casablanca en tant que principal pôle économique et financier du Royaume, de la diversification de son tissu économique ainsi que de sa capacité à attirer les investissements. Elle reflète également la qualité des dispositifs de planification financière et de suivi de l’exécution budgétaire mis en place par la Commune, ainsi que la mobilisation de mécanismes de financement diversifiés pour soutenir ses projets structurants. Le Plan d’Action Communal 2023-2028 et les programmes de développement du Grand Casablanca constituent, à cet égard, des leviers majeurs pour accompagner la transformation urbaine, améliorer la mobilité, renforcer les infrastructures et les services publics et contribuer à l’amélioration du cadre de vie des citoyens, souligne la même source. La perspective stable attribuée par S&P Global Ratings reflète celle du Royaume du Maroc, relève-t-on. Selon les projections de l’agence, la Commune devrait maintenir des performances budgétaires satisfaisantes au cours de la période 2026-2028, tout en poursuivant la réduction progressive de son endettement direct. Le rapport souligne également la solidité de la position de liquidité de la Commune et son accès à des sources de financement diversifiées. Cette notation constitue un repère important pour le dialogue avec les partenaires institutionnels et financiers et contribue à renforcer la visibilité de la Commune auprès des acteurs économiques et des investisseurs. La Commune de Casablanca réaffirme son engagement en faveur d’une gestion rigoureuse, transparente et responsable des finances publiques locales. Elle poursuivra ses efforts en matière de mobilisation des ressources, de rationalisation des dépenses, de maîtrise de l’endettement et d’optimisation de l’investissement public. Ces orientations s’inscrivent dans une démarche durable visant à consolider les équilibres financiers de la Commune, à renforcer sa capacité d’investissement et à accompagner les ambitions de développement économique, social et urbain de Casablanca. La Commune de Casablanca, conclut on, entend ainsi poursuivre la consolidation de ses acquis financiers au service d’une métropole plus attractive, plus résiliente et plus durable. items.title: GIMPA Law Students’ Association organises breast cancer awareness campaign, calls for regular screening
items.description: The Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) Law Students’ Association (LSA) has organised a breast cancer awareness campaign to educate students on the importance of regular breast self-examination, early detection and timely medical attention. The initiative, held as part of activities marking Breast Cancer Awareness Month in October, formed part of the Association’s efforts to promote health awareness and the general well-being of students within the university community. Speaking during the campaign, the President of the Law Students’ Association, Melchiah S.K. Mortty, encouraged women not to allow fear to prevent them from examining their breasts or seeking medical attention when they notice unusual changes. He explained that not every breast lump is cancerous and urged women to seek professional medical assessment rather than assume the worst or avoid examination out of fear. The Secretary of the Association, Josephine Tetteh, also encouraged women to regularly examine their breasts and pay attention to any unusual changes. She stressed the importance of being familiar with one’s body to help identify changes that may require medical attention. Adding his voice, the Organising Secretary of the Association, Abubakar Tanko Saddiq Nuhu, emphasised that breast cancer awareness should not end with October. He called for continuous efforts to sustain the campaign beyond Breast Cancer Awareness Month, noting that early detection can save lives. The President of the GIMPA Students’ Representative Council (SRC), Valerie Elikem Kportufe, and the SRC Vice President, Oswald Nii Aba, also joined the event in support of the awareness campaign. The Vice President of the Law Students’ Association, Cecil Adrian Sampson, was also present at the event. The campaign formed part of the GIMPA Law Students’ Association’s commitment to keeping students informed about important health issues, particularly breast cancer awareness and the importance of early detection. The Association hopes to sustain awareness beyond October and encourage students to remain conscious of their breast health throughout the year.

items.title: Critic of Mali’s Junta Forcibly Disappeared Six Months On
items.description: Click to expand Image Lawyer and junta critic Mountaga Tall, Mali, 2025. © Private Six months after their abductions, Mountaga Tall, an outspoken critic of Mali’s junta, and his son, Cheick Mamadou Tall, remain missing, their fate unknown, and the Malian authorities silent. Every day that passes without news raises fears for their safety and deepens their family’s anguish. Unidentified gunmen abducted Tall in Bamako, Mali’s capital, on May 2. Tall’s son went missing on May 16 after receiving a call informing him that he could deliver belongings to his father, who was reportedly being held at an undisclosed location. Radio France Internationale reported in July that the United Nations Committee on Enforced Disappearances had urged Mali’s authorities to locate and protect Tall and his son. International media suggest that Malian intelligence services may be holding Tall in a secret facility. Malian authorities, however, have neither acknowledged detaining Tall or his son nor provided information about their location, legal status, or health, despite requests from Tall’s family and a legal team. Tall, who was a government minister between 2014 and 2017, was initially aligned with Mali’s military authorities but later emerged as a critic of the junta who opposed the military-led government’s dissolution of political parties. The disappearances of Tall and his son fit a broader crackdown on political opposition, media and dissent under Mali’s military junta, which seized power in 2021. Authorities have suspended and banned media outlets, dissolved civil society groups, ended multiparty politics and subjected critics to arbitrary detention and enforced disappearance. Since Tall’s abduction, other political figures and their relatives have reportedly been abducted by masked gunmen, a modus operandi associated with Malian intelligence services and some remain missing. Under international human rights law, an enforced disappearance occurs when state authorities or their agents detain a person and then refuse to acknowledge the detention or disclose the person’s fate or whereabouts, thereby placing the person outside the protection of the law. Victims of enforced disappearance face a heightened risk of torture and execution. Enforced disappearance inflicts profound suffering on families, leaving them uncertain about whether their loved ones are alive or dead and denying them justice. Malian authorities should immediately disclose the whereabouts of Mountaga Tall and his son, ensure their safety, and release them.

items.title: Quintessential capitalism
items.description: FEW companies are hailed as proof of free-market genius more than Tesla. Yet, at every turn that mattered, it stood on public capital. In 2010 it borrowed $465m from a US federal programme open to every carmaker building cleaner vehicles, in a country where transport is now the largest source of greenhouse gases. It paid the Treasury’s own cost, roughly one to 3.4 per cent, with principal deferred until production began. One of the smallest borrowers, it became the star, repaying with interest nine years early. Regulatory credits, earned by beating emission rules and bought by those that fall short, then carried it into profit. Pakistan asks its banks to do alone what no quintessential capitalist economy asks of its own: lend to priority sectors without the state sharing the risk and the price. This is not a lesson taken from state-led economies such as China, where public support is part of the model. It comes from the market economies themselves, which do it openly and without apology. Tesla is not their exception; it is their method. Look at where they aim interest subsidies, and how deep. Farming comes first: America lends beginning farmers money to buy land at under 2pc and caps their operating microloans at 5pc, while Canada pays the interest on the first C$250,000 of each grower’s cash advance. Housing is next: France gives first-time buyers zero-interest loans and compensates banks through tax credits. Then enterprise: Britain lends start-ups unsecured at a fixed 6pc, with mentoring, and its firms outlive their peers; Germany’s KfW cheapens founders’ loans and absorbs four-fifths of any loss so local banks will lend. In every case, the taxpayer took the first risk and part of the financing cost, at the stage private finance would not, and demanded performance in return. And the subsidy went to the borrower, the priority-sector player, not the lender: the bank is paid only the market interest the borrower is spared. Subsidies have built giants, and an emerging economy needs them more, not less. That is the global norm. Why, then, is Pakistan so averse to it? Here, subsidy for producers is treated as a dirty word, subsidised credit is misread as a benefit to banks, and lenders are blamed for holding back from risks their peers abroad never shoulder unaided. Asking them to match the world’s lending without the world’s toolkit is neither fair nor realistic. The money exists; its direction is the problem. This year’s federal budget allocates Rs838bn to the Benazir Income Support Programme, up by a sixth, and almost as much to the power sector; provincial budgets add their own spending on wheat, fertiliser and household relief. Little of it is designed to make the poor bankable. BISP is indispensable. Reaching some 10 million families through a national registry and digital payments, it is one of the country’s institutional achievements, and that safety net must stay. But a stipend, by its nature, protects rather than transforms. A net that never becomes a springboard keeps the poor safe, but poor. BISP must now be balanced with wealth creation at the lower strata of society, so that families able to work have a path from support to enterprise. Wealth, like subsidy, is not a bad word. It can be created at every level, including the bottom, and it is what keeps incomes rising sustainably. The cliché about wealth must go, just like subsidies. So add a ramp without lowering the floor: dedicate a tenth of BISP’s allocation to an enterprise window within the programme; that is smaller than this year’s increase, so no family need receive less than last year. Run it as the world does. Target precisely: older people, persons with disabilities and households with no working member keep their full stipend; working-age households, starting with the women BISP serves, get concessional credit for livestock, horticulture, cottage industry, solar trades and digital work. Price it for the borrower: the first loan interest-free and repeat loans at no more than 5pc, the state paying the difference. Pay for delivery: lenders earn the subsidy only for verified results, and every loan comes with training and a mentor. Build the exit: the stipend tapers only once the business stands, and the subsidy steps down with each cycle. Even at today’s rates, that tenth could carry some Rs400bn of lending: over a million small businesses. Audit it independently after three years; scale it only if it works. Two objections deserve answers. Credit alone, global trials show, raises poor families’ incomes only modestly; what lifts them for good is capital paired with training and continued support while the business finds its feet, which is this design. Nor does the window raid BISP: it is paid for from the programme’s growth and serves the same households. It is time to retire the reflex that subsidies never create wealth or welfare. Bad design is bad; subsidy is not, if it pays for the initial risk rather than permanent inefficiency. Subsidies have built giants, and an emerging economy needs them more, not less. Washington’s decisive bet on Tesla was not a stipend but a loan, tied to milestones. Pakistan’s Teslas are smaller — a woman’s dairy herd, a tailor’s workshop, a graduate’s laptop — but they deserve the same deal: capital to start, conditions to keep, and a way out. Then the cycle begins again with the next borrower. That is routine in every quintessential capitalist economy, and it should be in Pakistan too. The writer is a development-focused and impact-oriented banker. Published in Dawn, October 30th, 2026

items.title: US plans to ban Chinese telecom firms from direct access to US phone numbers
items.description: The United States plans to ban Chinese telecom firms from direct access to US phone numbers soon on national security grounds—a measure designed to prevent scam-related robocalls. The US Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it will vote on November 19 on a proposal to ban China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom, and other IP-enabled service providers from direct access. For telecom firms providing Voice over Internet Protocol — technology that ⁠converts voice into digital data and transmits it over broadband connections — direct access is a ​much cheaper option and makes it easier to offer advanced features. “With this decision, the FCC will ​be strengthening our first line of defence against bad actors and illegal robocallers,” FCC Chair Brendan Carr said in a statement. The Chinese Embassy did not immediately comment. The FCC also said on Thursday that it plans ​to bar IP-enabled service providers that use equipment from companies on the FCC’s list that ​pose national security risks, including Huawei or ZTE. The agency added that it would ban all Chinese labs from ‌testing ⁠US electronics in December 2028 and may also revoke direct number authorizations for Chinese companies that it deems to pose national security risks. The FCC has previously barred China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom from providing international telecommunications services to the United States. Other measures under consideration include barring them from connecting to US networks and operating their data centres in the US. Concerns about potential spying and other harms arising from Chinese access to US telecom data and infrastructure have grown in recent years. In late 2024, Washington said ​a Chinese ⁠state-sponsored cyber espionage group known as Salt Typhoon stole consumers’ call records, US call data and infiltrated US telecommunications and telecom infrastructure firms. The FBI said this year that threats from Salt Typhoon are “still ⁠very ​much ongoing.” In July, the FCC added California-based Digitalsystem Technology to ​a list of companies posing risks to US national security, citing links to Chinese telecom firms and its ownership ​by a Chinese national. China has consistently denied any wrongdoing.

items.title: Candid admission
items.description: PARLIAMENT has recently been debating the future of Pakistani democracy, but those debates will be for naught unless our leaders also develop the capacity to acknowledge each other’s positions. The past two days have seen the government and opposition benches trading blame for democracy’s present, rather sorry state. On Wednesday, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman accused the government of misusing the Constitution and resorting to unconstitutional measures. He also said his party was “prepared to die” resisting the government if the latter continued pursuing a policy of confrontation and violence, and proposed a new Charter of Democracy as the way out. Regretting that his efforts to mediate between the government and the PTI had failed because the government had changed course and imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in KP, the maulana said the political leadership had grown too intolerant for parliament to do its job. He was not wrong, though the fault is hardly the government’s alone. The maulana’s rebuke drew two kinds of response. Minister of Defence Khawaja Asif resorted to personal attacks , insinuating that the JUI-F chief was merely sore at being denied a share of power in KP. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, on the other hand, was more circumspect. Though he, too, laid much of the blame for parliament’s dysfunction on the opposition, he nonetheless urged it to exercise its powers and return to parliamentary committees. “Those who want this House to remain dysfunctional and do not want the people of Pakistan to benefit from it have succeeded,” he told the opposition benches. “You have played a part in helping these people achieve their objective.” It was a surprisingly candid admission that the House’s dysfunction serves interests other than the people’s, even if the PPP chief left out his own party’s role in getting us here. They may have yet to come to terms with it, but both ruling and opposition parties have lost credibility and political ground due to their ongoing vendetta. The maulana’s call for a new Charter of Democracy, though welcome, looks difficult to realise when the two sides cannot even agree to sit together in parliamentary committees. The imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP was a gross misstep by the federal government, and it has spoiled the chances of a negotiated settlement. But the opposition, too, has gained little from confrontation. Unless both sides start to show some flexibility on key matters, make compromises and enter negotiations without preconditions, they risk further deepening this crisis of their own making. If enough lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are willing to admit that matters have gone too far, there may yet be hope for parliament, and for Pakistani democracy. The question is, are they ready to do so? Published in Dawn, October 30th, 2026

items.title: ‘Lawfare’ emerges as new threat to journalists in Pakistan
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan remained deeply hostile to journalism and its practitioners in 2025-26 despite a decline in documented violations against media workers, according to a new report issued by an Islamabad-based media watchdog. “About 10 cases a month [against media personnel], their nationwide spread and severity in the period showed that fewer violations did not mean greater safety,” stated Freedom Network’s latest annual Impunity Report 2026, titled “From Violence to Lawfare: Process as Punishment for Journalists”. Produced with technical assistance from International Media Support (IMS), the report was authored by journalist Adnan Rehmat and Freedom Network Executive Director Iqbal Khattak. It finds that “impunity has evolved from a failure to punish violence into a broader system of coercion”. Peca increasingly used to punish dissent, says Freedom Network report The report was released on Thursday ahead of the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists, observed worldwide, including in Pakistan, on Nov 2 each year. “Despite the presence on the statute books of two laws to combat impunity for crimes against journalists, such a finding should be a matter of concern for those at the helm of affairs of the two safety commissions established under these laws,” Mr Khattak said. Cases documented between October 2025 and August 2026 included one work-related killing, three attempted assassinations, 18 threats of murder or harm, 11 assaults, 13 legal actions and 32 threats of legal action. Punjab recorded 49 cases, just over half the total, followed by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Islamabad and Balochistan. Digital and independent journalists were targeted most often. Victims or their families identified government authorities and officials as alleged instigators in nearly two-thirds of the cases. The report identifies the controversial Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) and its increasing use against journalists by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to punish dissent as “central to this legal siege” of online journalism in the country. ‘Recurring pattern’ A detailed analysis of representative Peca-related cases against journalists reveals a recurring pattern in which allegations of defamation, false information, harassment or reputational harm are channelled through cybercrime procedures, including in cases involving reporting on public expenditure, corruption or official conduct. Even without a confirmed FIR or conviction, the process itself becomes “punitive” through summonses, device scrutiny, travel, legal costs, detention, repeated hearings, and reputational harm, the report says. It adds that relief is commonly limited to bail or procedural protection rather than final vindication. The report also provides guidelines for journalists and other media practitioners facing Peca-related cases to help minimise the harmful effects of legal action. It expresses concern over the lack of institutional safeguards for media workers despite the establishment of two high-powered safety commissions, one at the federal level and the other in Sindh. “The federal journalist protection mechanism is effectively dysfunctional, while the Sindh Commission, although more visible, has limited reach and demonstrated protection impact outside Karachi,” it says. Published in Dawn, October 30th, 2026

items.title: Lawmakers voice alarm over KP situation, seek electoral reforms
items.description: • Achakzai questions govt’s handling of Tehran diplomacy, Afghanistan ties • Senate resolution seeks coordinated national action to curb population growth ISLAMABAD: Lawmakers in the National Assembly and Senate on Thursday raised concerns over the political situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and alleged human rights violations, while both houses also discussed electoral reforms and the need to strengthen parliamentary institutions. National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai criticised the government for failing to take parliament into confidence over recent diplomatic developments in Tehran. “How can four people decide the future of the whole nation?” he asked, warning that such decisions could push the country towards “anarchy and civil war”. Mr Achakzai also opposed the suspension of trade with Afghanistan, describing Afghans as traditional friends of Pakistan and criticising the country’s past policies towards its neighbour. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said the parliamentary proceedings and the prevailing political situation in KP were creating a negative impression among the public. He also called for an end to hereditary politics in the country. Rights concerns raised Meanwhile, speaking on a point of order in the Senate, PTI parliamentary leader Barrister Syed Ali Zafar accused the government of undermining constitutional protections through the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP. He argued that fundamental human rights could not be suspended or compromised, regardless of the political situation. “There is one thing that cannot be broken, suspended or compromised: the fundamental human rights of the people of Pakistan,” he said. Mr Zafar expressed concern over the detention of Noreen Niazi, sister of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, claiming that she had suffered a heart attack and was hospitalised but her family was not being allowed to meet her. Responding to the concerns, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said Noreen Niazi had been provided medical treatment in Lahore and was in satisfactory condition. On allegations that her family was being denied access, Mr Sanaullah assured the house that details would be sought and the matter addressed according to the circumstances. He defended her detention, alleging that she had sought to create unrest by mobilising people for a protest march towards Islamabad. Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas also criticised the government’s actions in KP, alleging that the province had been “snatched from the people”. He also questioned the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, arguing that democratic institutions could not function without respect for the law. Population growth resolution Separately, the Senate passed a resolution calling for urgent and coordinated national action to address the challenges posed by the country’s rapidly growing population. The resolution, moved by PPP Vice President Senator Sherry Rehman, called for a comprehensive national response to population growth and its impact on public services and socioeconomic development. Ms Rehman said Pakistan’s population was projected to reach approximately 390 million by 2050 at the current growth rate, placing unprecedented pressure on national resources. Published in Dawn, October 30th, 2026

items.title: Netanyahu's bloc finishes ahead in Israel election, but well short of majority
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a majority, final results from general election showed on Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote. Netanyahu’s coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, with his Likud party remaining the largest faction with 27 seats. The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot, secured 48 seats. The results from the Central Elections Committee also cemented the emergence as potential kingmakers of the Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List, with the two winning a combined 19 seats. The fragmented outcome sets the stage for difficult negotiations to form a government that could last weeks, with no single bloc able to reach the 61-seat threshold needed and the prospect of another election remaining if talks fail. The final tally came after Netanyahu’s camp spent Thursday amplifying unproven allegations that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding to influence the vote, accusations rejected by both Arab-majority lists and Qatar. Israel’s Shin Bet domestic security service said it was investigating suspected irregularities, but stressed the probe was not intended to “cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote in a democratic and lawful manner”. The electoral commission also sought to calm tensions, with its acting director general Dean Livne saying any suggestion of widespread issues was “entirely groundless”. Political earthquake The controversy centred on allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas, to finance vote-buying operations. “The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party alleged on Thursday. Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing and welcomed an investigation, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu and his allies of conducting a “campaign of incitement” out of fear of Arab voters’ growing political influence. Government officials have so far provided no evidence to back the allegations. Opposition figures accused Netanyahu of attempting to undermine confidence in the results after failing to secure a governing majority. “He is trying to challenge the election results,” left-wing candidate Yair Golan said. Eisenkot said he was briefed by the Shin Bet and the election committee, adding it was “too early to understand what happened, and whether anything happened at all”. But he continued: “It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election.” Netanyahu himself has long been under the cloud of allegations related to Qatar after the arrests last year of two of his aides for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf state. Qatar called the latest accusations “ridiculous and dangerous”. Kingmakers under pressure Yousef Jabareen, head of the Joint List, told AFP that he is willing to cooperate with the opposition to bring down Netanyahu but without joining it in a government. Netanyahu had tried during the voting to raise allegations of fraud, saying that Arab parties were caught with envelopes of cash, and Likud peddled the accusations throughout Thursday. Police said they arrested three suspects but the election commission called it an isolated local case.

items.description: La consternation s'est emparée du quartier Kennedy 2, à Daloa, dans la nuit du mardi 27 au mercredi 28 octobre 2026. D. Lou Fabienne, dite « Fabi », gérante de maquis âgée de 26 ans originaire de Bahoulifla (près de Vavoua), a perdu la vie dans son domicile de deux pièces lors d'une violente altercation avec son concubin, S. Arthur, un boulanger du même âge. Alors que des rumeurs alarmantes et des récits contradictoires ont circulé dans le voisinage sur le mode opératoire, le suspect — retrouvé en pleurs près de la dépouille avant d'être interpellé par les forces de l'ordre — a affirmé avoir asséné un coup de bouteille à la tempe de sa compagne sur fond de soupçons d'infidélité. Informé, le procureur de la République a confié l'enquête à la Brigade de recherche et d'intervention (BRI) de Daloa afin de démêler le vrai du faux et d'établir avec exactitude les circonstances de ce crime. Le quartier Kennedy 2 de Daloa s'est réveillé dans la stupeur et la douleur ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026. Dans une modeste maison de deux pièces, le corps sans vie de D. Lou Fabienne, affectueusement appelée « Fabi » par ses proches, a été retrouvé gisant sur le sol du salon. Âgée de 26 ans, cette jeune femme originaire de Bahoulifla localité située à 16 kilomètres de Vavoua — y gérait un maquis et partageait le quotidien de son compagnon, S. Arthur, boulanger également âgé de 26 ans. Au petit matin, alertés par des pleurs et des bruits suspects, des voisins ont découvert le jeune homme prostré près de la dépouille de sa compagne, baignant dans le sang, avant que les forces de police ne soient alertées et ne procèdent à son interpellation sur les lieux. Selon les témoignages recueillis auprès de l'entourage, le ménage traversait une période d'intenses turbulences nourries par des scènes de jalousie récurrentes. Arthur nourrissait des soupçons persistants d'infidélité à l'encontre de sa partenaire, des accusations que Fabi avait constamment rejetées. Si les précédentes disputes finissaient d'ordinaire par s'apaiser, celle de la nuit du 27 au 28 octobre a franchi le point de non-retour. Selon les premières déclarations attribuées au suspect devant les enquêteurs, le ton est monté au cours d'une nouvelle dispute. L'homme se serait alors saisi d'une bouteille et aurait violemment frappé la jeune femme à la tempe. Sous la force de l'impact, la gérante de maquis s'est effondrée lourdement au sol sans pouvoir être ranimée. Dans le quartier, l'émoi suscité par la découverte du corps a rapidement alimenté les commentaires les plus sombres. Certains récits de voisinage et rumeurs ont évoqué un acte d'une cruauté inouïe, prétendant que la victime aurait été égorgée avant que son sang ne soit recueilli, tandis que d'autres témoins rapportent que l'auteur présumé aurait pris une douche et changé ses vêtements maculés avant de s'effondrer en larmes. Face à ces versions, les autorités judiciaires privilégient la rigueur des constatations matérielles et médico-légales. Le procureur de la République a officiellement saisi la Brigade de recherche et d'intervention (BRI) de Daloa pour mener les investigations. Les enquêteurs de la BRI sont désormais chargés d'auditionner les témoins, d'analyser les indices prélevés sur les lieux et de reconstituer la chronologie exacte des faits pour situer les responsabilités pénales devant la justice. L’article Drame conjugal à Daloa : La belle « Fabi », 26 ans, gérante de maquis tuée par son compagnon après une nuit de violences est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Ouagadougou : 24 mois de prison dont 6 ferme pour attentat à la pudeur sur une mineure de 15 ans
items.description: Un maçon de nationalité étrangère âgé de vingt-deux ans, P.K., a été condamné mardi par le Tribunal de grande instance Ouaga I à vingt-quatre mois d’emprisonnement, dont six mois ferme, et à une amende de cinq cent mille francs CFA avec sursis, pour attentat à la pudeur sur une adolescente de quinze ans. Initialement poursuivi pour viol, il a bénéficié d’une requalification des faits, le tribunal estimant que les éléments du dossier ne permettaient pas d’établir sa culpabilité pour cette infraction. (Attention : photos générées par IA). À la barre, P.K. a nié les faits de viol. Il a affirmé entretenir une relation amoureuse avec l’adolescente depuis près de trois mois, après l’avoir rencontrée près de son domicile alors qu’il travaillait sur un chantier dans un quartier périphérique de Ouagadougou. « La première fois que nous avons couché ensemble, c’était un vendredi. Je lui ai demandé et elle a accepté », a déclaré le prévenu, affirmant n’avoir découvert l’âge de la jeune fille qu’ensuite. Il a indiqué lui avoir offert des bijoux et avoir eu plusieurs rapports sexuels avec elle. « Je ne l’ai pas forcée », a-t-il soutenu. L’adolescente a contesté cette version. Elle a raconté avoir accompagné une amie, un jour de mariage, pour récupérer des plats dans la concession où vivait le prévenu. Celui-ci l’aurait alors entraînée de force à l’intérieur en lui couvrant la bouche, tandis que son colocataire refermait la porte. « Je ne pouvais pas crier. On s’est battus et il a eu le dessus. Il m’a violée », a-t-elle déclaré en mooré. Elle a ajouté être rentrée chez elle vers 21 heures, où sa mère l’a battue, et n’avoir pu raconter les faits à sa famille que le lendemain. Son père a alors saisi les autorités compétentes. Le tribunal lui a notamment demandé si la crainte de la réaction de ses parents ne l’avait pas poussée à évoquer un viol, ce qu’elle a rejeté. Les juges l’ont également interrogée sur les circonstances de l’agression, alors que son amie et le colocataire se trouvaient à l’extérieur. Les témoignages recueillis au cours de l’enquête ont conforté la version du prévenu. Son colocataire a confirmé ses déclarations, tandis que l’amie de l’adolescente a indiqué s’être rendue sur les lieux avec deux autres camarades. Le père de la jeune fille n’a formulé aucune réclamation, privilégiant le pardon, et s’en est remis au tribunal. Faute d’éléments suffisants pour établir le viol, le procureur du Faso a requis la requalification des faits en attentat à la pudeur, rappelant que la loi interdit les relations sexuelles avec des mineurs. Le tribunal a suivi le parquet. Source : Agence d’information du Burkina L’article Ouagadougou : 24 mois de prison dont 6 ferme pour attentat à la pudeur sur une mineure de 15 ans est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Pakistan’s climate defences under scrutiny amid Lancet warning
items.description: • Ex-health officials slam country’s ‘too little, too late’ disaster response; demand climate-proof hospitals, early warnings, heat action plans • Study calls for climate change to be declared global health emergency • Heat-related deaths rise 36pc since Paris accord; economic losses estimated at over $1tr ISLAMABAD: Health and environmental experts in Pakistan have called for urgent measures to address growing climate-related health risks after a Lancet report warned that rising heat-related deaths, floods, droughts and economic losses are outpacing global efforts to combat climate change. The 2026 Lancet Countdown report, launched at the British Library in London, called for climate change to be recognised as a “global health emergency”, warning that climate-related health risks continue to worsen a decade after the Paris Agreement. The report found that average annual heat-related deaths worldwide have risen 36 per cent since the Paris Agreement. In 2023, heat was linked to a record 710,000 deaths, with more than 70pc attributed to human-caused climate change. Meanwhile, heat-related economic losses reached an estimated $1.07 trillion in 2025. Former Punjab health minister Professor Dr Javed Akram told Dawn that the warning was particularly urgent for Pakistan, where the devastating 2022 floods displaced communities, damaged health care infrastructure, disrupted access to essential medicines and increased the risk of waterborne diseases and malnutrition. “Extreme heat further threatens vulnerable populations, particularly children, older adults, outdoor workers and people living with chronic illnesses,” he said. Mr Akram criticised Pakistan’s disaster management approach, saying policies had historically been reactive rather than proactive, with preparations beginning only after disasters strike. “Pakistan must strengthen heat-health action plans, establish effective early-warning systems, climate-proof hospitals, improve disease surveillance, and expand access to safe water and sanitation,” he said. He urged federal and provincial governments to allocate dedicated funding for climate-resilient health care and called on international partners to provide predictable, grant-based climate finance. Former special assistant to the prime minister on health Dr Zafar Mirza also warned that climate change had become a growing public health emergency in Pakistan. “Extreme heat, flash floods, cloud bursts and worsening air quality cause illness and death, while disrupting healthcare, contaminating water, undermining nutrition and deepening poverty and psychological distress,” he told Dawn. Dr Mirza said Pakistan needed climate-resilient health facilities, stronger disease surveillance, early-warning systems and coordinated action across health, climate, water, energy and finance. Dr Muhammad Irfan Khan, professor of environmental science and former dean at International Islamic University, expressed concern that Lancet Countdown’s launch statement did not mention Pakistan despite its exposure to climate-related disasters. “Pakistan’s experience should inform global priorities, research and investment,” he said, citing Germanwatch’s Climate Risk Index 2025, which ranked Pakistan as the country most affected by extreme weather in 2022. He urged international institutions to give greater visibility to vulnerable countries and ensure affected communities help shape climate responses. Published in Dawn, October 30th, 2026

items.title: Trump at odds with reports of Vance’s letter to Iran
items.description: • President says outreach focused on medical supplies, not peace talks • Tehran confirms receiving vice president’s letter, no response yet • US media claims correspondence sought to avert new strikes TEHRAN: Iranian media reported on Thursday that Tehran had received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance but had not yet responded, amid efforts to revive peace talks between the countries, though President Donald Trump said the outreach was about helping the country get medical supplies. Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency reported that “Iran has received the letter, but has not yet responded,” while the Fars news agency carried a similar account, citing “a source familiar with the matter.” The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times reported on Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter, that Vance had sent the letter to Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei at Trump’s direction in a bid to revive peace negotiations and avert new US strikes. The letter and subsequent contact between US and Iranian officials focused on a possible framework for negotiations rather than specific terms for a peace deal, the Journal reported. When asked by reporters later on Wednesday if he directed Vance to reach out to Iran to restart peace negotiations, Trump said, “No”. “What that is is they need help with medical supplies and various things. He asked me what I thought. I said, if you want to do that, that’s OK. Basically, it’s getting supplies in to help people that are not well,” Trump told reporters. Iran’s mission to the United Nations in New York and Vance’s office did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the letter and Trump’s remark. The reported correspondence comes as diplomatic efforts to end the war have yet to produce a lasting agreement. On Wednesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran was discussing a plan with mediators, mainly Qatar and Pakistan, to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a waterway that normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption. Qatari mediators presented Iran with a new draft deal Sunday to end the war, but a senior Iranian official said Doha had only put forward unacceptable ideas that did not amount to an offer. Tehran insists that Washington meet seven conditions it has set for reopening the strait. The conditions include a ceasefire across the Middle East, the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade. Tasnim reported that “any position that undermines this firm framework established by Iran is unacceptable”. The war began Feb 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran that assassinated former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and senior military commanders. Iran retaliated with attacks on Israel and US assets in the region, while the US imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports to starve it of oil export revenue. Iran has long blamed US sanctions for hindering civilian access to medical supplies. Published in Dawn, October 30th, 2026

items.description: Le général de corps d’armée Amadou Aya Sanogo, de l’Armée de terre, a été désigné président du Conseil d’administration de l’Office national des anciens combattants, militaires retraités et victimes de guerre du Mali (ONAC). Cette nomination a été officialisée par un décret signé le 22 octobre 2026 par le président de la Transition, chef de l’État, le général d’armée Assimi Goïta. Selon le décret, cette désignation s’inscrit dans le cadre des textes législatifs et réglementaires régissant l’organisation de la Défense et de la Sécurité, ainsi que le statut général des militaires. Le document précise également que le général Amadou Aya Sanogo bénéficiera, dans le cadre de ses nouvelles fonctions, des avantages prévus par la réglementation en vigueur. Le décret stipule enfin que toutes les dispositions antérieures contraires sont abrogées et que le texte sera enregistré et publié au Journal officiel. Cette nomination place ainsi le général Amadou Aya Sanogo à la tête de l’organe chargé de l’administration de l’ONAC, une structure consacrée aux anciens combattants, aux militaires retraités et aux victimes de guerre au Mali. items.title: Spain train crash impact speed up to 200 km/h, report suggests
items.description: The Renfe high-speed train that crashed into the back of a stationary Iryo service in Spain's Toledo province was traveling at an estimated 160 to 200 kilometers per hour at impact, according to the first preliminary report into the incident. Spain's Independent Administrative Authority for the Technical Investigation of Rail, Maritime and Civil Aviation Accidents and Incidents (AITAT) published the report on its website on Thursday, one day after the collision near Urda on the high-speed line connecting Madrid with the southern region of Andalusia. It said the exact speed will not be confirmed until data is extracted from the trains' on-board recorders. According to the report, the leading carriage of the Renfe AVE train, carriage 8, ploughed into the rear carriage of the Iryo train, carriage 1, and those two carriages overturned nose-down at the foot of the embankment and sustained the worst damage in the crash. The third carriage of the Renfe train – the third from the rear in the direction of travel – was pierced by a fragment of buckled rail, the report found, and on the Iryo train, all carriages except the first two, carriages 7 and 8, derailed, with the last three tumbling down the embankment. Investigators have documented a failure of the line's LZB automatic train protection and supervision system that began at 8:31 a.m., the report said. With the system offline, trains operated under an alternative working regime relying on lineside signals and the lateral signalling block. Controllers and drivers were required to exchange instructions by telephone. The report said a "chain of failures, instructions and actions" is believed to have led to the collision, with necessary safety mitigation barriers not activated. The authority stressed the investigation is at an early stage. Its next step will be to analyze the causes and circumstances behind the accident, examining possible environmental, organizational and procedural factors that could have mitigated or amplified the failures, alongside the signalling breakdown that created the risk. It emphasized it is too early to determine the exact cause. AITAT has up to one year to release its final findings. As of Thursday, 69 people died in the crash, according to the latest figures from Spain's emergency coordination center. Fifty injured people remain hospitalized.
